partyFact.title: A Buddhist crossroads
partyFact.text: Long before its modern borders, Afghanistan was a meeting place of Buddhist artistic traditions. The Bamiyan Valley preserves monasteries and sanctuaries spanning centuries of that history.

history.text: Not a conventional colony. Britain constrained Afghan foreign relations after 1879; Afghanistan regained full control in 1919. The Soviet invasion and military occupation lasted 1979–1989.

economy.description: Agriculture, local trade and small-scale industry support livelihoods; aid and remittances are important external sources of income.
economy.industries: small-scale production of bricks, textiles, soap, furniture, shoes, fertilizer, apparel, food products, non-alcoholic beverages, mineral water, cement; handwoven carpets; natural gas, coal, copper
economy.exports: coal, grapes, tropical fruits, gum resins, other nuts (2023)

partyFact.title: One town, several civilizations
partyFact.text: At Butrint, a walk through the ruins passes through a Greek colony, a Roman city and a bishopric. Marshes eventually helped bring this once-busy town to abandonment.

history.text: Ottoman rule covered most of the area from the late 1400s to independence in 1912. Italy occupied Albania in 1939–1943, followed by Nazi Germany in 1943–1944.

economy.industries: food; footwear, apparel and clothing; lumber, oil, cement, chemicals, mining, basic metals, hydropower
economy.exports: garments, footwear, electricity, crude petroleum, iron alloys (2023)

partyFact.title: The Sahara has a picture archive
partyFact.text: Tassili n’Ajjer holds more than 15,000 prehistoric drawings and engravings. They record changing animals, people and climate in a landscape that looks very different today.

history.text: France conquered Algiers in 1830 and expanded control inland over the following decades. French colonial rule ended with independence in 1962, after an eight-year war.

economy.industries: petroleum, natural gas, light industries, mining, electrical, petrochemical, food processing
economy.exports: natural gas, crude petroleum, refined petroleum, fertilizers, iron bars (2023)

partyFact.title: A valley that takes up a country-sized slice
partyFact.text: Andorra’s Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley covers about 9% of the whole country. Its mountain landscape still reflects a communal land-ownership tradition dating to the 13th century.

history.text: A special case: joint lordship began in 1278. French and Spanish-linked co-princes governed under the old arrangement until the 1993 constitution established parliamentary democracy; the co-princes remain heads of state.

economy.industries: tourism (particularly skiing), banking, timber, furniture
economy.exports: paintings, integrated circuits, cars, orthopedic appliances, garments (2023)

partyFact.title: A capital built around a sacred tree
partyFact.text: Mbanza Kongo was a capital of the Kingdom of Kongo. Its historic centre grew around a royal residence, a court and a holy tree, placing sacred and political landmarks together.

history.text: Portuguese colonial expansion began with coastal settlements in the 1500s, including Luanda in 1575. Control over the interior came much later. Angola became independent in 1975.

economy.industries: petroleum; diamonds, iron ore, phosphates, feldspar, bauxite, uranium, and gold; cement; basic metal products; fish processing; food processing, brewing, tobacco products, sugar; textiles; ship repair
economy.exports: crude petroleum, diamonds, natural gas, ships, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: A harbour designed by nature
partyFact.text: Antigua’s deep, narrow bays and surrounding hills made a natural hurricane shelter for sailing ships. That geography helped determine where the British built their naval dockyard, using enslaved African labour.

history.text: English settlement began in 1632. British colonial rule, interrupted briefly by France in 1666–1667, ended with independence in 1981.

economy.industries: tourism, construction, light manufacturing (clothing, alcohol, household appliances)
economy.exports: refined petroleum, ships, soybean meal, shellfish, paintings (2023)

partyFact.title: Trees older than the Roman Empire
partyFact.text: The alerce trees protected in Los Alerces National Park belong to a species that can live for more than 3,600 years. Some Patagonian forests are living records measured in millennia.

history.text: Spain colonised parts of the region from the 1500s. The Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata existed from 1776; revolution began in 1810 and independence was declared in 1816.

economy.industries: food processing, motor vehicles, consumer durables, textiles, chemicals and petrochemicals, printing, metallurgy, steel
economy.exports: soybean meal, corn, trucks, soybean oil, crude petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: Medieval book-making schools
partyFact.text: Sanahin monastery was famous for its calligraphers and manuscript illuminators. These Armenian monasteries were centres of learning as well as places of worship.

history.text: Russian imperial expansion brought eastern Armenian territories under its rule in the early 1800s. After independence in 1918–1920, Soviet rule began in 1920 and ended in 1991.

economy.description: Services, mining, food processing and trade support the economy, alongside money sent home by Armenians abroad.
economy.industries: brandy, mining, diamond processing, metal-cutting machine tools, forging and pressing machines, electric motors, knitted wear, hosiery, shoes, silk fabric, chemicals, trucks, instruments, microelectronics, jewelry, software, food processing
economy.exports: gold, diamonds, copper ore, broadcasting equipment, jewelry (2023)

partyFact.title: An annual meeting of ocean giants
partyFact.text: Whale sharks gather at Western Australia’s Ningaloo Coast every year. The same protected landscape also has a hidden world of underground caves and streams beneath the land.

history.text: British colonisation began in 1788, displacing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. Federation created a self-governing Commonwealth in 1901; legal independence developed in stages, culminating in the Australia Acts of 1986.

economy.industries: mining, industrial and transportation equipment, food processing, chemicals, steel
economy.exports: iron ore, coal, natural gas, gold, minerals (2023)

partyFact.title: A zoo in an imperial garden
partyFact.text: Schönbrunn’s palace gardens contain the zoo founded in 1752. The grounds bring an imperial residence and an extraordinarily long zoological history into the same place.

history.text: Nazi Germany annexed Austria in 1938 and ruled until 1945. Allied occupation then lasted from 1945 to 1955, when a state treaty restored full sovereignty.

economy.description: One of the strongest EU and euro economies.
economy.industries: construction, machinery, vehicles and parts, food, metals, chemicals, lumber and paper, electronics, tourism
economy.exports: cars, packaged medicine, vaccines, vehicle parts/accessories, nitrogen compounds (2023)

partyFact.title: A forest with a prehistoric pedigree
partyFact.text: The Hyrcanian forests shared by Azerbaijan and Iran trace their history back 25–50 million years. They are remnants of forests that once spread much more widely across northern temperate regions.

history.text: The Russian Empire absorbed the area in the early 1800s. Independence in 1918–1920 was followed by Soviet rule from 1920 to 1991.

economy.industries: petroleum and petroleum products, natural gas, oilfield equipment; steel, iron ore; cement; chemicals and petrochemicals; textiles
economy.exports: crude petroleum, natural gas, refined petroleum, plastics, electricity (2023)

partyFact.title: A pirate-friendly address
partyFact.text: The Bahamas’ position beside busy shipping lanes helped piracy flourish in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Its island geography made it useful for more than beach holidays.

history.text: English settlers arrived in 1648; formal royal colonial government began in 1718. Following a brief Spanish occupation in 1782–1783, British rule continued until independence in 1973.

economy.description: Tourism and financial services are the main engines of an economy closely connected to North American visitors and markets.
economy.industries: tourism, banking, oil bunkering, maritime industries, transshipment and logistics, salt, aragonite, pharmaceuticals
economy.exports: refined petroleum, ships, aluminum, shellfish, plastics (2023)

partyFact.title: Thousands of ancient towers for the dead
partyFact.text: Bahrain’s Dilmun heritage site includes roughly 11,774 burial mounds. Many were originally low cylindrical towers, built between about 2200 and 1750 BCE.

history.text: British protection developed through nineteenth-century treaties, especially the agreement of 1861. It ended with independence in 1971; the local Al Khalifa dynasty remained in power.

economy.description: Finance, petroleum refining and aluminium production diversify an economy historically built around oil.
economy.industries: petroleum processing and refining, aluminum smelting, iron pelletization, fertilizers, Islamic and offshore banking, insurance, ship repairing, tourism
economy.exports: refined petroleum, aluminum, iron ore, aluminum wire, jewelry (2023)

partyFact.title: Tiger country at the edge of the sea
partyFact.text: The Sundarbans is a maze of tidal channels and salt-tolerant mangroves where Bengal tigers live alongside crocodiles. A tiger habitat does not have to look like an inland jungle.

history.text: Bengal came under British East India Company control after 1757 and later British Crown rule. From 1947 to 1971, the area was East Pakistan; Bangladesh became independent in 1971.

economy.description: Garment exports bring in foreign earnings, while agriculture, domestic services and remittances support millions of households.
economy.industries: cotton, textiles and clothing, jute, tea, paper, cement, fertilizer, sugar, light engineering
economy.exports: garments, footwear, fabric, textiles, trunks and cases (2023)

partyFact.title: A city that refused the grid
partyFact.text: Bridgetown’s historic streets curve and wind. That layout sets it apart from the orderly grids used for many Spanish and Dutch colonial cities in the Caribbean.

history.text: English settlement began in 1627. The island remained under British colonial rule until independence in 1966, and became a republic in 2021.

economy.industries: tourism, sugar, light manufacturing, component assembly for export
economy.exports: liquor, refined petroleum, packaged medicine, margarine, baked goods (2023)

partyFact.title: A castle made from ten buildings
partyFact.text: Nesvizh Castle is an interconnected complex of ten buildings arranged around a six-sided courtyard. Its owners helped turn the town into a centre of art, science and craftsmanship.

history.text: Much of present-day Belarus passed from the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth to Russia in the partitions of 1772–1795. Soviet rule followed the revolutionary era; Nazi occupation interrupted it in 1941–1944. Independence came in 1991.

economy.description: Declining Russian energy subsidies will end in 2024.
economy.industries: metal-cutting machine tools, tractors, trucks, earthmovers, motorcycles, synthetic fibers, fertilizer, textiles, refrigerators, washing machines and other household appliances
economy.exports: fertilizers, rapeseed oil, wood, poultry, beef (2023)

partyFact.title: Lifts for boats
partyFact.text: Belgium’s historic Canal du Centre has four hydraulic boat lifts. They are the surviving examples of their era that UNESCO identifies as remaining in their original working condition.

history.text: The territory passed through Spanish and Austrian Habsburg rule before French annexation in 1795–1814 and union with the Netherlands in 1815–1830. Belgium became independent in 1830; German occupations followed in 1914–1918 and 1940–1944.

economy.description: High-income, core EU and eurozone economy.
economy.industries: engineering and metal products, motor vehicle assembly, transportation equipment, scientific instruments, processed food and beverages, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, base metals, textiles, glass, petroleum
economy.exports: refined petroleum, natural gas, vaccines, cars, packaged medicine (2023)

partyFact.title: A reef on a continental scale
partyFact.text: Belize’s coast forms part of the largest barrier reef in the Northern Hemisphere. The protected system includes not just coral, but atolls, mangroves, lagoons and hundreds of sandy cays.

history.text: British settlement developed from the 1600s. British Honduras became a crown colony in 1862 and achieved independence as Belize in 1981.

economy.industries: garment production, food processing, tourism, construction, oil
economy.exports: raw sugar, bananas, fish, shellfish, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: A last stronghold for West African lions
partyFact.text: Benin shares the W-Arly-Pendjari protected complex with Burkina Faso and Niger. UNESCO identifies it as the home of the region’s only viable lion population.

history.text: France conquered the Kingdom of Dahomey in the 1890s and established colonial rule. Independence came in 1960; the country adopted the name Benin in 1975.

economy.industries: textiles, food processing, construction materials, cement
economy.exports: gold, cotton, coconuts/brazil nuts/cashews, soybeans, wood (2023)

partyFact.title: A dance inspired by a vision
partyFact.text: Drametse’s famous masked drum dance traces its origin to a sixteenth-century religious vision. The tradition spread to other parts of Bhutan and became a major expression of its cultural heritage.

history.text: Bhutan was not formally colonised. A 1910 treaty gave Britain influence over external affairs until 1947; a related arrangement with independent India began in 1949 and was revised in 2007.

economy.industries: cement, wood products, processed fruits, alcoholic beverages, calcium carbide, tourism
economy.exports: iron alloys, aircraft, dolomite, semi-finished iron, cement (2023)

partyFact.title: A mountain that powered an industry
partyFact.text: In the 1500s, Potosí was an enormous silver-production centre. Artificial lakes and aqueducts supplied water to mills processing ore from Cerro Rico—the “Rich Mountain.”

history.text: Spanish conquest began in the 1530s. The colonial region known as Upper Peru became independent as Bolivia in 1825.

economy.description: Resource-rich economy benefits during commodity booms.
economy.industries: mining, smelting, electricity, petroleum, food and beverages, handicrafts, clothing, jewelry
economy.exports: gold, natural gas, precious metal ore, zinc ore, soybean meal (2023)

partyFact.title: A cave full of living fossils
partyFact.text: Vjetrenica Cave shelters animals whose nearest relatives disappeared long ago. It is also home to the only known subterranean tubeworm described in UNESCO’s account of the site.

history.text: Ottoman conquest began in 1463. Austria-Hungary administered Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1878 and annexed it in 1908; that rule ended in 1918. It later formed part of Yugoslavia until independence in 1992.

economy.industries: steel, coal, iron ore, lead, zinc, manganese, bauxite, aluminum, motor vehicle assembly, textiles, tobacco products, wooden furniture, ammunition, domestic appliances, oil refining
economy.exports: footwear, electricity, garments, plastic products, insulated wire (2023)

partyFact.title: An art gallery in the desert
partyFact.text: Tsodilo holds more than 4,500 rock paintings in just 10 square kilometres of the Kalahari. The landscape records human activity stretching back at least 100,000 years.

history.text: Britain established the Bechuanaland Protectorate in 1885. Protectorate status ended with independence as Botswana in 1966.

economy.description: Good economic governance and financial management.
economy.industries: diamonds, copper, nickel, salt, soda ash, potash, coal, iron ore, silver; beef processing; textiles
economy.exports: diamonds, copper ore, insulated wire, carbonates, cattle (2023)

partyFact.title: Brazil has more than rainforest
partyFact.text: The Cerrado is an ancient tropical savannah ecosystem. Its protected areas have sheltered species through past climate shifts, making this less-famous Brazilian landscape a remarkable refuge.

history.text: Portuguese colonisation followed the arrival of 1500. Brazil declared independence in 1822 and initially remained a monarchy under a branch of the Portuguese royal family.

economy.industries: textiles, shoes, chemicals, cement, lumber, iron ore, tin, steel, aircraft, motor vehicles and parts, other machinery and equipment
economy.exports: soybeans, crude petroleum, iron ore, raw sugar, corn (2023)

partyFact.title: A neighbourhood over the river
partyFact.text: Kampong Ayer is a large settlement of houses on stilts over the Brunei River. Wooden walkways link parts of the community, while boats connect it to the surrounding city.

history.text: Brunei became a British protectorate in 1888. Japanese occupation interrupted this in 1941–1945; full independence came in 1984 while the sultanate continued.

economy.description: Almost exclusively an oil and gas economy.
economy.industries: petroleum, petroleum refining, liquefied natural gas, construction, agriculture, aquaculture, transportation
economy.exports: refined petroleum, natural gas, crude petroleum, hydrocarbons, fertilizers (2023)

partyFact.title: Half-human, half-plant sculptures
partyFact.text: Inside the ancient Thracian tomb at Sveshtari, ten carved female figures blend human and plant forms. The tomb dates to the third century BCE but was only discovered in 1982.

history.text: Ottoman conquest was completed in the late 1300s. Bulgaria gained autonomy in 1878 and declared full independence in 1908. Soviet troops occupied the country in 1944–1947.

economy.industries: electricity, gas, water; food, beverages, tobacco; machinery and equipment, automotive parts, base metals, chemical products, coke, refined petroleum, nuclear fuel; outsourcing centers
economy.exports: refined petroleum, garments, refined copper, wheat, natural gas (2023)

partyFact.title: Iron-making before the Roman Empire
partyFact.text: At Douroula, evidence of iron production dates to the eighth century BCE. Burkina Faso’s heritage sites also preserve standing furnaces from later iron-working traditions.

history.text: French conquest in the late 1890s brought the territory into its colonial empire. Upper Volta was constituted as a colony in 1919, later reorganised, and became independent in 1960; it was renamed Burkina Faso in 1984.

economy.industries: cotton lint, beverages, agricultural processing, soap, cigarettes, textiles, gold
economy.exports: gold, cotton, oil seeds, coconuts/brazil nuts/cashews, cement (2023)

partyFact.title: Drumming with a moving centre
partyFact.text: Burundi’s royal-drum ritual combines percussion, dancing, songs and heroic poetry. Drums form a semicircle around a central drum, with some performers dancing to the ensemble’s rhythm.

history.text: German colonial rule was established in the 1890s. Belgium occupied the area in 1916 and later administered Ruanda-Urundi under international mandates and trusteeship. Burundi became independent in 1962.

economy.industries: light consumer goods (sugar, shoes, soap, beer); cement, assembly of imported components; public works construction; food processing (fruits)
economy.exports: gold, coffee, tea, tin ores, iron bars (2023)

partyFact.title: Cambodian temples before Angkor
partyFact.text: Sambor Prei Kuk has more than 100 temples, including ten unusual octagonal ones. The site belonged to an earlier Khmer capital that flourished before the famous Angkor period.

history.text: Cambodia was a French protectorate from 1863 to 1953. Japanese influence and occupation disrupted French control in 1941–1945. Vietnamese military intervention and troop presence lasted 1978–1989.

economy.description: Garment manufacturing, tourism, construction and agriculture are important sources of jobs and income.
economy.industries: tourism, garments, construction, rice milling, fishing, wood and wood products, rubber, cement, gem mining, textiles
economy.exports: garments, semiconductors, trunks and cases, footwear, gold (2023)

partyFact.title: A river almost wraps a rainforest
partyFact.text: The Dja River nearly encircles Cameroon’s Dja Faunal Reserve. This natural boundary surrounds a rainforest refuge with more than a hundred recorded mammal species.

history.text: Germany established Kamerun in 1884; its rule ended during World War I in 1916. France and Britain then administered separate territories. French Cameroon became independent in 1960, joined by British Southern Cameroons in 1961.

economy.description: Largest CEMAC economy with many natural resources.
economy.industries: petroleum production and refining, aluminum production, food processing, light consumer goods, textiles, lumber, ship repair
economy.exports: crude petroleum, natural gas, gold, cocoa beans, wood (2023)

partyFact.title: Tropical-sea fossils in Quebec
partyFact.text: Anticosti Island preserves marine fossils spanning roughly ten million years around Earth’s first major animal mass extinction. Today’s Canadian island was once beneath an ancient tropical sea.

history.text: French colonisation began in the early 1600s; Britain acquired most of New France in 1763. Confederation in 1867 created a self-governing dominion. Legislative autonomy followed in 1931, and constitutional patriation in 1982.

economy.description: High-income economy and second-largest US trading partner.
economy.industries: transportation equipment, chemicals, processed and unprocessed minerals, food products, wood and paper products, fish products, petroleum, natural gas
economy.exports: crude petroleum, cars, gold, natural gas, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: An Atlantic town with an early tropical chapter
partyFact.text: Cidade Velha, formerly Ribeira Grande, is identified by UNESCO as the first European colonial outpost in the tropics. Parts of its early street layout survive on Santiago island.

history.text: Portuguese settlement began in the 1460s on previously uninhabited islands. Colonial rule ended with Cabo Verde’s independence in 1975.

economy.industries: food and beverages, fish processing, shoes and garments, salt mining, ship repair
economy.exports: fish, refined petroleum, railway cargo containers, shellfish, garments (2023)

partyFact.title: A landscape that switches habitats
partyFact.text: Manovo-Gounda St Floris combines broad savannahs with northern floodplains. That contrast makes room for very different wildlife communities, from land mammals to waterbirds.

history.text: France established control in the late 1800s, organising Ubangi-Shari as a territory in 1903. The Central African Republic became independent in 1960.

economy.industries: gold and diamond mining, logging, brewing, sugar refining
economy.exports: gold, wood, diamonds, vehicle parts/accessories, cotton (2023)

partyFact.title: Fresh water in the Sahara
partyFact.text: Chad’s Ounianga site has 18 lakes fed by groundwater in an extremely dry desert. Some are salty, while others support freshwater fish; floating reeds help limit evaporation.

history.text: French conquest began around 1900; Chad became a separate colony in 1920. French colonial rule ended with independence in 1960.

economy.description: Oil-dependent economy challenged by market fluctuations, regional instability, refugee influx, and climate vulnerability.
economy.industries: oil, cotton textiles, brewing, natron (sodium carbonate), soap, cigarettes, construction materials
economy.exports: crude petroleum, gold, oil seeds, gum resins, cotton (2023)

partyFact.title: A town built around a staircase
partyFact.text: Sewell was built so high and steep in the Andes that wheeled vehicles were impractical. Its colourful mining-town buildings grew around a great central staircase instead.

history.text: Spanish conquest and settlement began in the 1540s, though Indigenous resistance limited control in the south. The independence process began in 1810, with independence proclaimed in 1818.

economy.industries: copper, lithium, other minerals, foodstuffs, fish processing, iron and steel, wood and wood products, transport equipment, cement, textiles
economy.exports: copper ore, refined copper, fish, carbonates, pitted fruits (2023)

partyFact.title: A rest stop for millions of birds
partyFact.text: China’s Yellow Sea and Bohai Gulf wetlands are a bottleneck on a huge migration route. Millions of waterbirds depend on this coastal stopping point between breeding and wintering grounds.

history.text: China was itself an imperial power. The Mongol-led Yuan dynasty ruled in 1271–1368 and the Manchu-led Qing in 1644–1912. Foreign concessions and Japanese occupations affected parts of China in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries; China as a whole was not one European colony.

economy.description: Manufacturing and exports are major strengths; domestic services, investment, construction and agriculture also support output.
economy.industries: world leader in gross value of industrial output; mining and ore processing, iron, steel, aluminum, and other metals, coal; machine building; armaments; textiles and apparel; petroleum; cement; chemicals; fertilizer; consumer products (including footwear, toys, and electronics); food processing; transportation equipment, including automobiles, railcars and locomotives, ships, aircraft; telecommunications equipment, commercial space launch vehicles, satellites
economy.exports: broadcasting equipment, computers, integrated circuits, garments, machine parts (2023)

partyFact.title: A shark gathering far offshore
partyFact.text: Around remote Malpelo island, observers have recorded groups of more than 200 hammerhead sharks and over 1,000 silky sharks. This little Colombian island sits about 506 km from the coast.

history.text: Spain conquered and colonised the region in the 1500s. Independence struggles began in 1810; the 1819 victory at Boyacá helped secure independence and the creation of Gran Colombia.

economy.description: Services support domestic activity, while petroleum, coal, coffee and other agricultural exports bring in foreign earnings.
economy.industries: textiles, food processing, oil, clothing and footwear, beverages, chemicals, cement; gold, coal, emeralds
economy.exports: crude petroleum, coal, gold, coffee, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: Island cities shaped by both family lines
partyFact.text: The historic Comorian sultanate towns developed with matrilineal and matrilocal customs alongside patrilineal Islamic traditions. Their streets and buildings reflect centuries of Indian Ocean cultural exchange.

history.text: French control began with Mayotte in 1841 and expanded through protectorates over other islands in 1886. Comoros declared independence in 1975. Mayotte remained under French administration, a status Comoros disputes.

economy.industries: fishing, tourism, perfume distillation
economy.exports: cloves, ships, essential oils, vanilla, scrap iron (2023)

partyFact.title: A rainforest far out in the Pacific
partyFact.text: Cocos Island lies about 550 km off Costa Rica. UNESCO identifies it as the tropical eastern Pacific’s only island with a tropical rainforest; underwater, it is famous for large ocean-going animals.

history.text: Spanish colonisation developed in the 1500s. Costa Rica declared independence from Spain in 1821, later leaving the Central American federation in 1838.

economy.industries: medical equipment, food processing, textiles and clothing, construction materials, fertilizer, plastic products
economy.exports: medical instruments, integrated circuits, orthopedic appliances, bananas, tropical fruits (2023)

partyFact.title: A cathedral with 71 faces
partyFact.text: The Cathedral of St James in Šibenik has a frieze of 71 sculpted faces of women, men and children. Its builders also constructed the cathedral entirely from stone.

history.text: Croatian lands experienced different Hungarian, Habsburg, Venetian and Ottoman rulers over centuries. Habsburg rule over much of the territory lasted 1527–1918. Croatia was later part of Yugoslavia until independence in 1991.

economy.industries: chemicals and plastics, machine tools, fabricated metal, electronics, pig iron and rolled steel products, aluminum, paper, wood products, construction materials, textiles, shipbuilding, petroleum and petroleum refining, food and beverages, tourism
economy.exports: ships, garments, electricity, packaged medicine, wood (2023)

partyFact.title: Plants that learned to live with toxic rock
partyFact.text: Some rocks in Alejandro de Humboldt National Park are chemically hostile to plants. Adaptation to those conditions helped produce a remarkable variety of species found nowhere else.

history.text: Spanish colonial rule began in 1511 and ended in 1898. A US military occupation followed in 1898–1902; Cuba became formally independent in 1902, with another US occupation in 1906–1909.

economy.description: Still largely state-run planned economy, although privatization increasing under new constitution.
economy.industries: petroleum, nickel, cobalt, pharmaceuticals, tobacco, construction, steel, cement, agricultural machinery, sugar
economy.exports: tobacco, nickel, liquor, zinc ore, precious metal ore (2023)

partyFact.title: Plain outside, spectacular inside
partyFact.text: The rural exteriors of some Troodos churches look modest. Inside, elaborate Byzantine and later murals cover the walls—a striking contrast preserved across ten listed monuments.

history.text: Ottoman rule lasted 1571–1878. Britain administered Cyprus from 1878 and formally annexed it in 1914. Independence came in 1960. The island has been divided since the Turkish military intervention of 1974.

economy.industries: tourism, food and beverage processing, cement and gypsum, ship repair and refurbishment, textiles, light chemicals, metal products, wood, paper, stone and clay products
economy.exports: ships, refined petroleum, packaged medicine, cheese, scented mixtures (2023)

partyFact.title: A landscape designed like a garden
partyFact.text: The Lednice-Valtice estate covers about 200 square kilometres. Its rulers reshaped whole stretches of countryside, combining castles and Baroque buildings with English-inspired romantic landscaping.

history.text: The Czech lands were under Habsburg rule from 1526 to 1918. Nazi Germany occupied the Czech lands in 1938–1945, with the Protectorate established in 1939. Czechoslovakia split peacefully into Czechia and Slovakia in 1993.

economy.industries: motor vehicles, metallurgy, machinery and equipment, glass, armaments
economy.exports: cars, vehicle parts/accessories, broadcasting equipment, computers, plastic products (2023)

partyFact.title: A river that brings a different habitat
partyFact.text: The Comoé River allows patches of rainforest to occur much farther north than expected. Its park mixes those forests with savannah vegetation in the same protected landscape.

history.text: France declared Côte d’Ivoire a colony in 1893 after earlier coastal treaties and settlements. Colonial rule ended with independence in 1960.

economy.description: One of West Africa’s most influential, stable, and rapidly developing economies.
economy.industries: foodstuffs, beverages; wood products, oil refining, gold mining, truck and bus assembly, textiles, fertilizer, building materials, electricity
economy.exports: gold, cocoa beans, rubber, refined petroleum, coconuts/brazil nuts/cashews (2023)

partyFact.title: A rainforest reached by water
partyFact.text: Salonga, described by UNESCO as Africa’s largest tropical rainforest reserve, is so isolated that access is by water. It protects animals such as bonobos and Congo peacocks.

history.text: The Congo Free State was controlled personally by Belgium’s King Leopold II from 1885 to 1908. Belgium then governed the Belgian Congo from 1908 until independence in 1960.

economy.description: Copper, cobalt and other minerals generate export earnings, while agriculture and small-scale trade support many livelihoods.
economy.industries: mining (copper, cobalt, gold, diamonds, coltan, zinc, tin, tungsten), mineral processing, consumer products (textiles, plastics, footwear, cigarettes), metal products, processed foods and beverages, timber, cement, commercial ship repair
economy.exports: refined copper, cobalt, copper ore, raw copper, crude petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: A prehistoric aquarium in the cliffs
partyFact.text: The cliffs of western Limfjord preserve exceptionally detailed fossil fish, along with turtles, birds and insects. These remains reveal how life responded to a major warming episode in the early Eocene.

history.text: Denmark was a regional kingdom and colonial power, rather than a modern overseas colony. Nazi Germany occupied it from 1940 to 1945.

economy.industries: wind turbines, pharmaceuticals, medical equipment, shipbuilding and refurbishment, iron, steel, nonferrous metals, chemicals, food processing, machinery and transportation equipment, textiles and clothing, electronics, construction, furniture and other wood products
economy.exports: packaged medicine, fish, vaccines, refined petroleum, pork (2023)

partyFact.title: A landscape of natural chimneys
partyFact.text: Around Lake Abbe, mineral deposits have built tall chimney-like rock formations. The hot-spring landscape looks industrial, but its towers are geological creations.

history.text: French footholds began with treaties in 1862; French Somaliland was established in 1896. Renamed the French Territory of the Afars and Issas in 1967, it became independent as Djibouti in 1977.

economy.description: Food import-dependent Horn of Africa economy driven by various national military bases and port-based trade.
economy.industries: construction, agricultural processing, shipping
economy.exports: raw sugar, seed oils, cars, palm oil, rice (2023)

partyFact.title: A lake that boils
partyFact.text: Dominica’s Morne Trois Pitons National Park contains a boiling lake, hot springs and dozens of steam vents. Its tropical forest grows across a remarkably active volcanic landscape.

history.text: France established colonial settlements in the 1600s and Britain obtained Dominica in 1763. After further conflict and a French occupation in 1778–1784, British rule continued until independence in 1978.

economy.industries: soap, coconut oil, tourism, copra, furniture, cement blocks, shoes
economy.exports: iron blocks, medical instruments, excavation machinery, power equipment, soap (2023)

partyFact.title: A city used as a planning template
partyFact.text: Santo Domingo’s colonial grid became a model for later towns across the Americas. UNESCO also records the city’s early cathedral, hospital, customs house and university as regional firsts.

history.text: Spain colonised Hispaniola from 1493. The eastern part passed through French control in 1795–1809, returned to Spain until 1821, and came under Haiti in 1822–1844. Independence was declared in 1844; Spain briefly reannexed it in 1861–1865 and the US occupied it in 1916–1924.

economy.description: Surging middle-income tourism, construction, mining, and telecommunications OECS economy.
economy.industries: tourism, sugar processing, gold mining, textiles, cement, tobacco, electrical components, medical devices
economy.exports: medical instruments, tobacco, gold, garments, power equipment (2023)

partyFact.title: Three currents, one evolutionary laboratory
partyFact.text: Three ocean currents meet around the Galápagos. Combined with volcanic activity and isolation, that setting helped produce the unusual wildlife that influenced Darwin after his 1835 visit.

history.text: Spanish conquest began in 1534. Victory over Spanish forces in 1822 brought the territory into Gran Colombia; Ecuador became a separate republic in 1830.

economy.industries: petroleum, food processing, textiles, wood products, chemicals
economy.exports: crude petroleum, shellfish, bananas, fish, gold (2023)

partyFact.title: Whales with legs—in the desert
partyFact.text: Egypt’s Whale Valley preserves fossils of early whales during their transition from land to sea. Some show the stage when these animals were losing their hind limbs.

history.text: Ottoman rule began in 1517, with increasing local autonomy later. Britain occupied Egypt in 1882 and imposed a formal protectorate in 1914–1922. Independence in 1922 was limited; British forces left the Suez Canal zone in 1956.

economy.description: Services, agriculture and industry support livelihoods; tourism, Suez Canal activity, energy and remittances earn foreign income.
economy.industries: textiles, food processing, tourism, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, hydrocarbons, construction, cement, metals, light manufactures
economy.exports: refined petroleum, natural gas, fertilizers, garments, crude petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: A farming village frozen by a volcano
partyFact.text: Joya de Cerén was buried by an eruption around 600 CE. Like Pompeii, its exceptional preservation offers a close look at ordinary lives—in this case a Central American farming community.

history.text: Spain conquered the region in the 1520s. Independence from Spain came in 1821; El Salvador later left the Central American federation in 1839.

economy.industries: food processing, beverages, petroleum, chemicals, fertilizer, textiles, furniture, light metals
economy.exports: garments, plastic products, electrical capacitors, raw sugar, toilet paper (2023)

partyFact.title: Spanish in Central Africa
partyFact.text: Spanish is one of Equatorial Guinea’s official languages, alongside French and Portuguese. That linguistic combination reflects a very different colonial history from many of its neighbours.

history.text: Portugal ceded its claims to Spain in 1778. Spanish colonial control developed unevenly over the islands and mainland and ended with independence in 1968.

economy.description: Oil and gas dominate export earnings and public revenue; this makes the economy sensitive to energy production and prices.
economy.industries: petroleum, natural gas, sawmilling
economy.exports: crude petroleum, natural gas, alcohols, wood, scrap iron (2023)

partyFact.title: Modernist architecture high in Africa
partyFact.text: Asmara sits more than 2,000 metres above sea level and preserves an extensive early-modernist cityscape. Cinemas, hotels and religious buildings reflect a major 1930s building programme under Italian colonial rule.

history.text: Italy established the colony of Eritrea in 1890 and lost it in 1941. British administration lasted 1941–1952, followed by federation with Ethiopia in 1952–1962 and Ethiopian annexation in 1962–1991. Formal independence came in 1993.

economy.description: Largely agrarian economy with a significant mining sector.
economy.industries: food processing, beverages, clothing and textiles, light manufacturing, salt, cement
economy.exports: copper ore, zinc ore, gold, garments, liquor (2023)

partyFact.title: A medieval trading city still readable today
partyFact.text: Tallinn’s old town grew rich through the Hanseatic trading network. Its surviving merchants’ houses and public buildings let you trace that commercial world through the streets.

history.text: Swedish and Russian rule followed earlier Danish and German control; the Russian Empire governed from 1721 to 1918. Soviet occupation in 1940–1941 was followed by Nazi occupation in 1941–1944 and renewed Soviet rule in 1944–1991.

economy.description: High-income, service-based EU and eurozone economy.
economy.industries: food, engineering, electronics, wood and wood products, textiles; information technology, telecommunications
economy.exports: cars, wood, broadcasting equipment, refined petroleum, prefabricated buildings (2023)

partyFact.title: A national anthem with two musical influences
partyFact.text: Eswatini’s anthem combines Swazi and western musical elements. Adopted at independence in 1968, it is a small musical record of traditions meeting.

history.text: British administration lasted from 1903 until independence in 1968. Previously known internationally as Swaziland, the kingdom adopted the name Eswatini in 2018.

economy.industries: soft drink concentrates, coal, forestry, sugar processing, textiles, and apparel
economy.exports: scented mixtures, raw sugar, industrial acids/oils/alcohols, garments, wood (2023)

partyFact.title: A goat with a very small world
partyFact.text: The Walia ibex is found only in Ethiopia’s Simien Mountains. The same landscape has cliffs dropping around 1,500 metres and wildlife adapted to its dramatic high-altitude terrain.

history.text: Ethiopia retained independence during most of Africa’s colonial era, defeating Italy at Adwa in 1896. Italy nevertheless invaded and occupied it from 1936 to 1941.

economy.description: Agriculture supports livelihoods and exports such as coffee; manufacturing, construction and services also contribute.
economy.industries: food processing, beverages, textiles, leather, garments, chemicals, metals processing, cement
economy.exports: coffee, garments, dried legumes, cut flowers, oil seeds (2023)

partyFact.title: Fiji’s first colonial capital was not Suva
partyFact.text: It was Levuka, a port town along the beach on Ovalau. Its layout grew around existing indigenous villages, whose residents continued to outnumber European settlers.

history.text: Fiji was ceded to Britain in 1874. British colonial rule ended with independence in 1970.

economy.description: Upper-middle income, tourism-based Pacific island economy.
economy.industries: tourism, sugar processing, clothing, copra, gold, silver, lumber
economy.exports: water, fish, raw sugar, refined petroleum, garments (2023)

partyFact.title: An industrial time capsule
partyFact.text: Verla preserves a rural paper-and-board mill settlement of a kind once widespread across northern Europe and North America. Only a handful of comparable settlements survived so completely.

history.text: Swedish rule developed during the medieval period and lasted until 1809. Finland then became an autonomous grand duchy under Russia from 1809 until independence in 1917.

economy.description: High-income, export-based EU and eurozone economy.
economy.industries: metals and metal products, electronics, machinery and scientific instruments, shipbuilding, pulp and paper, foodstuffs, chemicals, textiles, clothing
economy.exports: paper, refined petroleum, steel, wood pulp, ships (2023)

partyFact.title: France has a penguin chapter
partyFact.text: Remote French islands in the southern Indian Ocean support enormous colonies of king penguins. French geography reaches far beyond Europe into sub-Antarctic seas.

history.text: France was a major imperial power, rather than a modern overseas colony. Nazi Germany occupied much of it in 1940–1944; Vichy governed the initially unoccupied zone until German forces entered it in 1942.

economy.description: High-income, advanced EU economy and eurozone member.
economy.industries: machinery, chemicals, automobiles, metallurgy, aircraft, electronics, textiles, food processing, tourism
economy.exports: aircraft, cars, packaged medicine, gas turbines, vehicle parts/accessories (2023)

partyFact.title: Waterfalls with their own miniature worlds
partyFact.text: Ivindo National Park’s rivers and waterfalls shelter highly localised aquatic plants. UNESCO notes that parts remain little studied and some fish species have yet to be formally described.

history.text: French footholds began with coastal treaties in 1839–1841. Colonial control expanded in the later 1800s; Gabon became independent in 1960.

economy.description: Oil, manganese mining and forestry are major economic activities and sources of export income.
economy.industries: petroleum extraction and refining; manganese, gold; chemicals, ship repair, food and beverages, textiles, lumbering and plywood, cement
economy.exports: crude petroleum, ships, manganese ore, refined petroleum, wood (2023)

partyFact.title: A small island with a long historical reach
partyFact.text: Kunta Kinteh Island sits in the River Gambia. Its remains record successive chapters of African–European contact, including the slave trade and its abolition.

history.text: British colonial claims began in 1664, with later changes in boundaries and administration. The modern colony and protectorate became independent as The Gambia in 1965.

economy.industries: peanuts, fish, hides, tourism, beverages, agricultural machinery assembly, woodworking, metalworking, clothing
economy.exports: packaged medicine, cars, harvesting machinery, refined petroleum, trailers (2023)

partyFact.title: A monastery that was also an academy
partyFact.text: Founded in 1106, Gelati was a major centre of science and education in medieval Georgia. Its academy made the monastery a place for scholarship as well as worship.

history.text: The Russian Empire began annexing Georgian kingdoms in 1801. Independence in 1918–1921 was followed by Soviet conquest in 1921 and Soviet rule until 1991.

economy.description: Trade, transport, tourism and other services are important, alongside agriculture and money sent home from abroad.
economy.industries: steel, machine tools, electrical appliances, mining (manganese, copper, gold), chemicals, wood products, wine
economy.exports: cars, copper ore, electricity, garments, wine (2023)

partyFact.title: Ice Age people made music too
partyFact.text: Caves in Germany’s Swabian Jura have yielded musical instruments as well as carved animals and jewellery. The finds date back roughly 33,000–43,000 years.

history.text: After Nazi Germany’s defeat, the US, UK, France and USSR occupied separate zones from 1945. Two German states formed in 1949; occupation arrangements changed in 1955, and the remaining Four-Power rights were suspended at reunification in 1990 and formally ended in 1991.

economy.description: Leading export-driven, core EU and eurozone economy.
economy.industries: iron, steel, coal, cement, chemicals, machinery, vehicles, machine tools, electronics, automobiles, food and beverages, shipbuilding, textiles
economy.exports: cars, vehicle parts/accessories, packaged medicine, plastic products, vaccines (2023)

partyFact.title: An Atlantic archive built in stone
partyFact.text: Ghana’s coastal forts and trading posts were built across more than 300 years, from 1482 to 1786. Their remains mark successive phases of Atlantic trade and European expansion.

history.text: Britain established the Gold Coast colony in 1874 and later extended control over Asante and the north. The Gold Coast and British Togoland became independent as Ghana in 1957.

economy.industries: mining, lumbering, light manufacturing, aluminum smelting, food processing, cement, small commercial ship building, petroleum
economy.exports: gold, crude petroleum, cocoa beans, manganese ore, cocoa paste (2023)

partyFact.title: The gods had a real mountain address
partyFact.text: Mount Olympus is a real Greek mountain landscape, not merely a mythical place. Ancient writers made it the home of the Olympian gods, while its steep terrain shelters varied habitats.

history.text: Ottoman conquest spread across much of Greece in the 1400s. The independence war began in 1821; an independent Greek state was recognised in 1830, with later territorial additions. Axis occupation lasted 1941–1944.

economy.industries: tourism, food and tobacco processing, textiles, chemicals, metal products; mining, petroleum
economy.exports: refined petroleum, packaged medicine, aluminum, olive oil, tobacco (2023)

partyFact.title: An art gallery you snorkel through
partyFact.text: Grenada’s Molinere Beauséjour marine area contains an underwater sculpture gallery. The works draw on local culture, moving the idea of a museum visit beneath the sea.

history.text: French settlement began in 1649. Britain acquired Grenada in 1763, lost it to France in 1779, and regained it in 1783. British rule ended with independence in 1974.

economy.industries: food and beverages, textiles, light assembly operations, tourism, construction, education, call-center operations
economy.exports: nutmeg/cardamons, fish, wheat flours, frozen fruits and nuts, aqueous paints (2023)

partyFact.title: A crossroads between civilizations
partyFact.text: Tak’alik Ab’aj records about 1,700 years of history spanning the transition from Olmec to early Maya culture. Trade carried ideas through the site as well as goods.

history.text: Spanish conquest began in 1524. Guatemala declared independence from Spain in 1821 and subsequently belonged to a Central American federation before becoming a separate republic.

economy.industries: sugar, textiles and clothing, furniture, chemicals, petroleum, metals, rubber, tourism
economy.exports: garments, bananas, coffee, palm oil, raw sugar (2023)

partyFact.title: Tool-using chimpanzees and unusual toads
partyFact.text: Mount Nimba shelters chimpanzees that use stones as tools and a toad that gives birth to live young. Its mountain habitats rise above the surrounding savannah.

history.text: French colonial control expanded in the late 1800s; French Guinea became a colony in 1891. Guinea voted to leave the French colonial system and became independent in 1958.

economy.description: Mining, especially bauxite and gold, earns export revenue; agriculture supports many household livelihoods.
economy.industries: bauxite, gold, diamonds, iron ore; light manufacturing, agricultural processing
economy.exports: gold, aluminum ore, cocoa beans, crude petroleum, coconuts/brazil nuts/cashews (2023)

partyFact.title: An island stopover for a huge bird migration
partyFact.text: The Bijagós protected landscape supports over 870,000 migratory shorebirds. It is also part of the only active deltaic archipelago on Africa’s Atlantic coast.

history.text: Portuguese trading posts appeared in the 1400s, but conquest of the interior came much later. Guinea-Bissau declared independence in 1973, recognised by Portugal in 1974.

economy.industries: agricultural products processing, beer, soft drinks
economy.exports: coconuts/brazil nuts/cashews, fish, fish oil, processed crustaceans, malt extract (2023)

partyFact.title: A waterfall with a 226-metre plunge
partyFact.text: Kaieteur Falls drops about 226 metres in Guyana’s rainforest. It is an immense single plunge rather than a long staircase of smaller cascades.

history.text: Dutch colonies developed in the 1600s. Britain took control in the early 1800s, confirmed in 1814; British Guiana was consolidated in 1831. Independence came in 1966.

economy.description: Small, hydrocarbon-driven South American export economy.
economy.industries: bauxite, sugar, rice milling, timber, textiles, gold mining
economy.exports: crude petroleum, railway cargo containers, gold, ships, rice (2023)

partyFact.title: A fortress built after a revolution
partyFact.text: Haiti’s Citadel and Sans Souci belong to the years after independence. UNESCO recognises these monuments as symbols of the freedom won by formerly enslaved people.

history.text: France obtained the western part of Hispaniola from Spain in 1697. The Haitian Revolution began in 1791 and ended French colonial rule with independence in 1804. The US occupied Haiti in 1915–1934.

economy.description: Small Caribbean island economy and OECS-member state.
economy.industries: textiles, sugar refining, flour milling, cement, light assembly using imported parts
economy.exports: garments, essential oils, scrap iron, industrial acids/oils/alcohols, bedding (2023)

partyFact.title: Mountains that run down to the Caribbean
partyFact.text: The Río Plátano reserve links mountainous rainforest to the Caribbean shore. Its landscape is also a long-standing home for indigenous communities, rather than an uninhabited wilderness.

history.text: Spanish conquest developed from the 1520s. Independence from Spain came in 1821; Honduras left the Central American federation in 1838. British influence and claims affected the Caribbean coast separately.

economy.description: Manufacturing, agriculture and services support output; exports and remittances are important sources of foreign income.
economy.industries: sugar processing, coffee, woven and knit apparel, wood products, cigars
economy.exports: garments, coffee, insulated wire, palm oil, shellfish (2023)

partyFact.title: A school inside a thousand-year-old community
partyFact.text: Benedictine monks settled at Pannonhalma in 996 and established Hungary’s first school. The abbey’s long educational tradition continues alongside its monastic life.

history.text: Following the Ottoman victory in 1526, Hungary was divided between Ottoman, Habsburg and Transylvanian domains. Ottoman control in the centre lasted mainly 1541–1699; Habsburg rule continued until 1918. Germany occupied Hungary in 1944, followed by Soviet military domination after 1945.

economy.industries: mining, metallurgy, construction materials, processed foods, textiles, chemicals (especially pharmaceuticals), motor vehicles
economy.exports: cars, vehicle parts/accessories, electric batteries, packaged medicine, computers (2023)

partyFact.title: An island with a birth date
partyFact.text: Surtsey emerged from volcanic eruptions between 1963 and 1967. Protected from ordinary human disturbance, it lets scientists watch plants and animals colonise brand-new land.

history.text: Iceland came under Norway in 1262–1264 and later the Danish crown. It became a sovereign kingdom in union with Denmark in 1918 and a republic in 1944. British and then US forces were stationed there during World War II.

economy.industries: tourism, fish processing; aluminum smelting; geothermal power, hydropower; medical/pharmaceutical products
economy.exports: aluminum, fish, orthopedic appliances, animal meal, iron alloys (2023)

partyFact.title: Bridges made from living roots
partyFact.text: In Meghalaya, communities guide and weave the living roots of rubber fig trees across streams. Over time, the roots form usable bridges—a piece of infrastructure that is still alive.

history.text: Many regional kingdoms and empires preceded British expansion. East India Company control grew after 1757; direct British Crown rule lasted 1858–1947. Independence and partition came in 1947; princely states followed different arrangements.

economy.description: Services, including IT and business services, support a large domestic economy alongside manufacturing and agriculture.
economy.industries: textiles, chemicals, food processing, steel, transportation equipment, cement, mining, petroleum, machinery, software, pharmaceuticals
economy.exports: refined petroleum, packaged medicine, diamonds, broadcasting equipment, garments (2023)

partyFact.title: From tropical sea to snowy mountains
partyFact.text: Lorentz National Park spans environments from marine waters and wetlands to high mountain terrain shaped by glaciers. It is a startling reminder that Indonesia has an alpine world as well as tropical islands.

history.text: Dutch control developed gradually from the 1600s and never began everywhere at once. Japan occupied the islands in 1942–1945. Independence was proclaimed in 1945 and recognised by the Netherlands in 1949; western New Guinea followed a separate later process.

economy.description: A large domestic market supports services and manufacturing, alongside mining, energy and agricultural exports.
economy.industries: petroleum and natural gas, textiles, automotive, electrical appliances, apparel, footwear, mining, cement, medical instruments and appliances, handicrafts, chemical fertilizers, plywood, rubber, processed food, jewelry, and tourism
economy.exports: coal, palm oil, iron alloys, lignite, garments (2023)

partyFact.title: A thousand-year-old brick skyscraper
partyFact.text: Gonbad-e Qābus is a 53-metre tomb tower built in 1006. Its tapering cylinder and conical roof demonstrate sophisticated geometry using ordinary unglazed fired bricks.

history.text: Iran was itself a centre of empires, rather than a single modern European colony. Arab conquest occurred in the seventh century and Mongol conquest in the thirteenth. Britain and the USSR jointly occupied parts of Iran in 1941–1946.

economy.description: Oil and gas, manufacturing, agriculture and services support the economy; sanctions constrain international trade and finance.
economy.industries: petroleum, petrochemicals, gas, fertilizer, caustic soda, textiles, cement and other construction materials, food processing (particularly sugar refining and vegetable oil production), ferrous and nonferrous metal fabrication, armaments
economy.exports: plastics, iron ore, alcohols, natural gas, refined copper (2023)

partyFact.title: A wetland world in an arid country
partyFact.text: Southern Iraq’s Ahwar is a vast inland delta of marshes in a very hot, dry region. Nearby are the remains of Ur, Uruk and Eridu, cities of ancient Mesopotamia.

history.text: Ottoman rule covered much of the region from the 1500s until World War I. British occupation began during the war and a mandate followed in 1920; formal independence came in 1932. The US-led occupation authority governed in 2003–2004.

economy.description: Oil exports dominate public revenue and foreign earnings, making government spending highly sensitive to the energy sector.
economy.industries: petroleum, chemicals, textiles, leather, construction materials, food processing, fertilizer, metal fabrication/processing
economy.exports: crude petroleum, refined petroleum, petroleum coke, gold, natural gas (2023)

partyFact.title: Stone-age art on a monumental scale
partyFact.text: The Boyne Valley’s Newgrange, Knowth and Dowth form an exceptional concentration of prehistoric stone art. These monuments served social and ceremonial roles as well as burial functions.

history.text: English intervention began in 1169 and control expanded over centuries. The island was incorporated into the United Kingdom in 1801. Most of Ireland became the Irish Free State in 1922; Northern Ireland remained in the UK.

economy.industries: pharmaceuticals, chemicals, computer hardware and software, food products, beverages and brewing; medical devices
economy.exports: vaccines, packaged medicine, nitrogen compounds, integrated circuits, hormones (2023)

partyFact.title: Half a million years in four caves
partyFact.text: The Mount Carmel caves preserve evidence spanning at least 500,000 years of human evolution. Finds include both Neanderthals and early modern humans within the same broad prehistoric cultural tradition.

history.text: The territory was under Ottoman rule in 1517–1917. British military administration followed, then the British Mandate in 1923–1948. Israel declared independence in 1948. These dates describe rule over the territory before the modern state.

economy.industries: high-technology products (including aviation, communications, computer-aided design and manufactures, medical electronics, fiber optics), wood and paper products, potash and phosphates, food, beverages, and tobacco, caustic soda, cement, pharmaceuticals, construction, metal products, chemical products, plastics, cut diamonds, textiles, footwear
economy.exports: integrated circuits, diamonds, broadcasting equipment, medical instruments, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: A volcano with a very long written record
partyFact.text: Mount Etna’s activity has been documented for at least 2,700 years. Its much longer geological record reaches back roughly half a million years.

history.text: Before unification in 1861, the peninsula contained many states under different local and foreign rulers, including Spanish and Austrian dynasties. Nazi Germany occupied much of northern and central Italy in 1943–1945.

economy.industries: tourism, machinery, iron and steel, chemicals, food processing, textiles, motor vehicles, clothing, footwear, ceramics
economy.exports: packaged medicine, garments, cars, refined petroleum, vehicle parts/accessories (2023)

partyFact.title: Mountains that became a refuge
partyFact.text: Jamaica’s Blue and John Crow Mountains sheltered Taino people and later Maroon communities escaping slavery. Trails, settlements and forest knowledge helped communities resist colonial control.

history.text: Spanish colonial rule began in 1509. England seized Jamaica in 1655, and British rule continued until independence in 1962.

economy.industries: agriculture, mining, manufacture, construction, financial and insurance services, tourism, telecommunications
economy.exports: aluminum oxide, refined petroleum, natural gas, liquor, processed fruits and nuts (2023)

partyFact.title: Wooden buildings from the seventh century
partyFact.text: Some Buddhist buildings at Horyu-ji date to the late 600s or early 700s. They are among the world’s oldest surviving wooden structures—not stone ruins, but timber architecture.

history.text: Japan was not a European colony and became an imperial power itself. After defeat in World War II, an Allied occupation led by the US lasted from 1945 to 1952; some islands returned later.

economy.industries: motor vehicles, electronic equipment, machine tools, steel and nonferrous metals, ships, chemicals, textiles, processed foods
economy.exports: cars, integrated circuits, machinery, vehicle parts/accessories, construction vehicles (2023)

partyFact.title: Monks who lived on towers
partyFact.text: At Um er-Rasas, two surviving towers are associated with stylites: ascetic monks who isolated themselves on top of columns or towers. The site also contains elaborate mosaic floors.

history.text: The territory was under Ottoman rule from 1516 until 1918. The Emirate of Transjordan was established under British supervision in 1921 and became independent in 1946.

economy.industries: tourism, information technology, clothing, fertilizer, potash, phosphate mining, pharmaceuticals, petroleum refining, cement, inorganic chemicals, light manufacturing
economy.exports: fertilizers, garments, phosphates, jewelry, phosphoric acid (2023)

partyFact.title: A grand building left unfinished
partyFact.text: The Yasawi mausoleum was begun under Timur in 1389 and remained partly unfinished. Its builders tested architectural ideas later used in the empire’s great capital, Samarkand.

history.text: Russian imperial control expanded across the steppe from the 1700s through the 1800s. Soviet rule followed the revolutionary era; Kazakhstan was a union republic from 1936 until independence in 1991.

economy.industries: oil, coal, iron ore, manganese, chromite, lead, zinc, copper, titanium, bauxite, gold, silver, phosphates, sulfur, uranium, iron and steel; tractors and other agricultural machinery, electric motors, construction materials
economy.exports: crude petroleum, gold, radioactive chemicals, refined copper, copper ore (2023)

partyFact.title: A flamingo feeding destination
partyFact.text: Kenya’s Rift Valley lakes are crucial feeding grounds for lesser flamingos. Bogoria, Nakuru and Elementaita form a linked lake system supporting extraordinary bird diversity.

history.text: Britain established the East Africa Protectorate in 1895 and the Kenya colony in 1920. British rule ended with independence in 1963; earlier coastal history included Portuguese and Omani rule.

economy.description: Agriculture, trade, finance, telecommunications and tourism support the economy. Tea and cut flowers are important exports.
economy.industries: agriculture, transportation, services, manufacturing, construction, telecommunications, tourism, retail
economy.exports: tea, cut flowers, garments, gold, tropical fruits (2023)

partyFact.title: Mountains hidden under the Pacific
partyFact.text: Kiribati’s Phoenix Islands protected area includes 14 known underwater seamounts, thought to be extinct volcanoes. Its ocean habitats cover over 400,000 square kilometres.

history.text: The Gilbert Islands became a British protectorate in 1892 and part of a colony in 1916. Japan occupied some islands in 1941–1943. Kiribati became independent in 1979.

economy.industries: fishing, handicrafts
economy.exports: fish, coconut oil (2023)

partyFact.title: An oil economy that started saving early
partyFact.text: Kuwait is home to the oldest sovereign wealth fund. Its overseas investment tradition shows how an oil-producing country can turn resource revenue into assets beyond its own borders.

history.text: Kuwait was under British protection from 1899 to 1961, with local rulers retaining internal authority. Iraq invaded and occupied it from August 1990 until liberation in February 1991.

economy.description: Small, high-income, oil-based Middle East economy.
economy.industries: petroleum, petrochemicals, cement, shipbuilding and repair, water desalination, food processing, construction materials
economy.exports: crude petroleum, refined petroleum, natural gas, hydrocarbons, plastics (2023)

partyFact.title: A mountain home for fruit ancestors
partyFact.text: The Western Tien-Shan is an important centre of origin for cultivated fruit crops. These mountain forests are part of the deeper story behind familiar fruit on a dinner table.

history.text: Russian imperial conquest incorporated the territory during the 1800s. Soviet administration followed; Kyrgyzstan became a union republic in 1936 and independent in 1991.

economy.industries: small machinery, textiles, food processing, cement, shoes, lumber, refrigerators, furniture, electric motors, gold, rare earth metals
economy.exports: gold, coal, precious metal ore, refined petroleum, garments (2023)

partyFact.title: Two architectural worlds in one town
partyFact.text: Luang Prabang blends traditional Lao buildings and urban patterns with French colonial architecture. The combination is preserved across a whole townscape, not just a single landmark.

history.text: Laos was under French colonial rule from 1893 to 1953. Japanese intervention briefly displaced French power in 1945; the independence process then continued after the war.

economy.description: Lower middle-income, industrial Southeast Asian economy.
economy.industries: mining (copper, tin, gold, gypsum); timber, electric power, agricultural processing, rubber, construction, garments, cement, tourism
economy.exports: electricity, fertilizers, gold, garments, paper (2023)

partyFact.title: Survey markers that helped measure Earth
partyFact.text: Latvia is on the Struve Geodetic Arc, a 2,820-km chain of survey points across ten countries. Nineteenth-century measurements along it helped establish Earth’s size and shape.

history.text: Latvian territories passed through German, Polish–Lithuanian and Swedish control before incorporation into Russia during the 1700s. Independence in 1918 was followed by Soviet occupation in 1940–1941, Nazi occupation in 1941–1944/1945, and Soviet rule until 1991.

economy.industries: processed foods, processed wood products, textiles, processed metals, pharmaceuticals, railroad cars, synthetic fibers, electronics
economy.exports: wood, wheat, broadcasting equipment, packaged medicine, natural gas (2023)

partyFact.title: Trees once prized for great buildings
partyFact.text: Lebanon’s surviving cedar forests connect to an ancient building material traded and valued across the region. Nearby Qadisha’s monasteries cling to a dramatic mountain valley.

history.text: Ottoman rule lasted from 1516 until 1918. France established Greater Lebanon in 1920 and administered it under a mandate. Independence was declared in 1943; the last French troops withdrew in 1946.

economy.industries: banking, tourism, real estate and construction, food processing, wine, jewelry, cement, textiles, mineral and chemical products, wood and furniture products, oil refining, metal fabricating
economy.exports: jewelry, cars, diamonds, scrap iron, gold (2023)

partyFact.title: A mountain kingdom with rock-art galleries
partyFact.text: Lesotho shares the Maloti-Drakensberg landscape with South Africa. Its cliffs, caves and rock shelters preserve a remarkable concentration of paintings as well as highland wildlife.

history.text: Basutoland became a British protectorate in 1868. It was administered by the Cape Colony in 1871–1884, then directly by Britain until independence as Lesotho in 1966.

economy.description: Lower middle-income economy surrounded by South Africa.
economy.industries: food, beverages, textiles, apparel assembly, handicrafts, construction, tourism
economy.exports: diamonds, garments, wool, power equipment, bedding (2023)

partyFact.title: An anthem writer who became president
partyFact.text: Daniel Bashiel Warner wrote the words of Liberia’s national anthem. He later became the country’s third president—a rather unusual career change for a lyricist.

history.text: Liberia was founded through settlement sponsored by the American Colonization Society from 1822 and declared independence in 1847. It was not a US government colony; settler domination of Indigenous communities remained an important part of its history.

economy.industries: mining (iron ore and gold), rubber processing, palm oil processing, diamonds
economy.exports: gold, ships, iron ore, rubber, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: A desert city with streets under the houses
partyFact.text: In Ghadamès, homes overhang covered alleys, creating sheltered passageways. Traditionally, supplies were kept below, families lived above, and women used the open rooftop terraces.

history.text: Ottoman rule began in 1551 and ended with the Italian invasion in 1911. Italian colonial control lasted until defeat in 1943. British and French administrations governed different areas until independence in 1951.

economy.description: Upper middle-income, fossil fuel-based North African economy.
economy.industries: petroleum, petrochemicals, aluminum, iron and steel, food processing, textiles, handicrafts, cement
economy.exports: crude petroleum, natural gas, refined petroleum, gold, scrap iron (2023)

partyFact.title: A familiar tune with different words
partyFact.text: Liechtenstein’s national anthem uses the same melody as “God Save the King.” At an international sporting event, the tune can sound British even when the team is not.

history.text: The principality was created within the Holy Roman Empire in 1719 and became sovereign when that empire dissolved in 1806. It was not a modern overseas colony; close customs and diplomatic relationships with Austria and Switzerland did not make it part of those countries.

economy.industries: electronics, metal manufacturing, dental products, ceramics, pharmaceuticals, food products, precision instruments, tourism, optical instruments
economy.exports: small specialty machinery, connectors for audio and video, parts for motor vehicles, dental products, hardware

partyFact.title: A capital that transformed a provincial town
partyFact.text: Kaunas served as Lithuania’s provisional capital between the world wars. That role triggered a wave of modernist public buildings, homes and urban planning in just two decades.

history.text: Most of Lithuania was incorporated into Russia in 1795. Independence returned in 1918. Soviet occupation in 1940–1941 was followed by Nazi occupation in 1941–1944 and renewed Soviet rule until restoration of independence in 1990–1991.

economy.description: High-income EU and eurozone member, largest Baltic economy.
economy.industries: metal-cutting machine tools, electric motors, televisions, refrigerators and freezers, petroleum refining, shipbuilding (small ships), furniture, textiles, food processing, fertilizer, agricultural machinery, optical equipment, lasers, electronic components, computers, amber jewelry, information technology, video game development, app/software development, biotechnology
economy.exports: refined petroleum, furniture, plastic products, wheat, cars (2023)

partyFact.title: A fortress repeatedly upgraded by its owners
partyFact.text: Luxembourg’s strategic position made successive European powers reinforce its defences. Centuries of fortification ended with the dismantling of its walls beginning in 1867.

history.text: Luxembourg passed through Burgundian, Spanish, Austrian and French rule. From 1815 to 1890 it shared a monarch with the Netherlands while developing separate statehood. Germany occupied it in 1914–1918 and 1940–1944.

economy.description: Financial services and other business services are central, supported by cross-border trade and workers.
economy.industries: banking and financial services, construction, real estate services, iron, metals, and steel, information technology, telecommunications, cargo transportation and logistics, chemicals, engineering, tires, glass, aluminum, tourism, biotechnology
economy.exports: iron blocks, gas turbines, plastic products, rubber tires, plastics (2023)

partyFact.title: An evolutionary experiment lasting millions of years
partyFact.text: Madagascar’s long isolation helped its plants and animals evolve independently. Its eastern rainforests preserve part of that distinctive world, including rare lemurs.

history.text: France invaded in 1895 and annexed Madagascar in 1896. Colonial rule ended with independence in 1960.

economy.industries: meat processing, seafood, soap, beer, leather, sugar, textiles, glassware, cement, automobile assembly plant, paper, petroleum, tourism, mining
economy.exports: garments, nickel, vanilla, cloves, gold (2023)

partyFact.title: A mountain rising like an island
partyFact.text: Mount Mulanje is an enormous inselberg—a mountain mass rising above the surrounding landscape. For local communities, its water, rocks and forests also belong to a sacred landscape.

history.text: Britain proclaimed a protectorate in 1891, later named Nyasaland. It belonged to the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland in 1953–1963 and became independent as Malawi in 1964.

economy.industries: tobacco, tea, sugar, sawmill products, cement, consumer goods
economy.exports: tobacco, tea, dried legumes, soybean meal, raw sugar (2023)

partyFact.title: A room hundreds of metres wide—underground
partyFact.text: Sarawak Chamber in Gunung Mulu is about 600 metres long, 415 metres wide and 80 metres high. The surrounding cave network is home to millions of bats and swiftlets.

history.text: Different territories had different rulers: Britain acquired Penang in 1786 and progressively expanded control over Malaya and northern Borneo. Japanese occupation lasted 1941/1942–1945. Malaya became independent in 1957; Malaysia formed in 1963.

economy.industries: Peninsular Malaysia - rubber and oil palm processing and manufacturing, petroleum and natural gas, light manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, medical technology, electronics and semiconductors, timber processing; Sabah - logging, petroleum and natural gas production; Sarawak - agriculture processing, petroleum and natural gas production, logging
economy.exports: integrated circuits, refined petroleum, crude petroleum, natural gas, palm oil (2023)

partyFact.title: A cabinet meeting in scuba gear
partyFact.text: In October 2009, Maldivian ministers held a cabinet meeting four metres underwater. The event was designed to draw attention to climate change before the Copenhagen summit.

history.text: The Maldives was a British protectorate from 1887 until independence in 1965. Local sultans retained internal authority; a republic replaced the sultanate in 1968.

economy.description: Tourism is the principal economic engine, with fishing and related processing also important for jobs and exports.
economy.industries: tourism, fish processing, shipping, boat building, coconut processing, woven mats, rope, handicrafts, coral and sand mining
economy.exports: fish, aircraft, refined petroleum, scrap iron, natural gas (2023)

partyFact.title: A pyramid built from mud
partyFact.text: The Tomb of Askia in Gao has a striking 17-metre pyramidal form. Built in 1495, it reflects the wealth of the Songhai Empire and the Sahel’s monumental earthen-building tradition.

history.text: French conquest developed in the late 1800s; much of the territory was administered as French Sudan. Independence came through the Mali Federation in 1960, followed that year by the separate Republic of Mali.

economy.industries: food processing; construction; phosphate and gold mining
economy.exports: gold, cotton, oil seeds, fertilizers, gum resins (2023)

partyFact.title: Hundreds of monuments in a tiny capital
partyFact.text: UNESCO counts 320 monuments within Valletta’s 55 hectares. Malta’s capital packs an extraordinary amount of architectural history into a very small footprint.

history.text: The Knights of St John ruled Malta in 1530–1798. French occupation lasted 1798–1800, followed by British control from 1800 until independence in 1964.

economy.description: Tourism, financial and business services, manufacturing and trade support this small island economy.
economy.industries: tourism, electronics, ship building and repair, construction, food and beverages, pharmaceuticals, footwear, clothing, tobacco, aviation services, financial services, information technology services
economy.exports: refined petroleum, integrated circuits, packaged medicine, ships, postage stamps/documents (2023)

partyFact.title: History beneath a lagoon
partyFact.text: Bikini Atoll’s lagoon contains ships sunk during the 1946 nuclear tests. These underwater remains are part of a difficult history that also includes the displacement of the islanders.

history.text: Germany established a protectorate in 1885. Japan took control in 1914, followed by the US in 1944. US-administered UN trusteeship began in 1947; free association took effect in 1986 and trusteeship formally ended in 1990.

economy.description: US assistance, public services, fishing and related activities are major sources of income.
economy.industries: copra, tuna processing, tourism, craft items (from seashells, wood, and pearls)
economy.exports: ships, refined petroleum, fish, natural gas, stone processing machines (2023)

partyFact.title: Desert dunes meet a bird-filled sea
partyFact.text: At Banc d’Arguin, Sahara dunes sit beside shallow Atlantic waters, islands and coastal swamps. That abrupt meeting of desert and ocean creates a major wintering ground for migratory birds.

history.text: French control developed from the early 1900s; Mauritania became a colony in 1920. Colonial rule ended with independence in 1960.

economy.industries: fish processing, oil production, mining (iron ore, gold, copper)
economy.exports: gold, iron ore, fish, processed crustaceans, copper ore (2023)

partyFact.title: A mountain that became a symbol of freedom
partyFact.text: Escaped enslaved people sheltered on Le Morne’s wooded cliffs and in its caves. Their history gave this Mauritian mountain a meaning far beyond its dramatic outline.

history.text: Dutch settlement lasted intermittently from 1638 to 1710. France took possession in 1715; Britain captured the island in 1810 and ruled until independence in 1968.

economy.description: Upper middle-income Indian Ocean island economy.
economy.industries: food processing (largely sugar milling), textiles, clothing, mining, chemicals, metal products, transport equipment, nonelectrical machinery, tourism
economy.exports: fish, garments, raw sugar, fertilizers, diamonds (2023)
