partyFact.title: A forest made of cacti
partyFact.text: The Tehuacán-Cuicatlán Valley has exceptionally dense forests of tall columnar cacti. It also preserves ancient canals, wells and dams that supported early agricultural settlements.

history.text: Spanish conquest of the Aztec capital in 1521 began the colonial era of New Spain. Independence came in 1821. A French intervention supported a short-lived empire in 1862–1867.

economy.industries: food and beverages, tobacco, chemicals, iron and steel, petroleum, mining, textiles, clothing, motor vehicles, consumer durables, tourism
economy.exports: cars, vehicle parts/accessories, crude petroleum, trucks, computers (2023)

partyFact.title: A city built on artificial islets
partyFact.text: Nan Madol is spread across more than 100 constructed islets off Pohnpei. Walls of basalt and coral boulders supported palaces, temples and homes built between roughly 1200 and 1500.

history.text: Spain claimed the Caroline Islands and sold them to Germany in 1899. Japan took control in 1914; US control followed during World War II. A US-administered trusteeship began in 1947; free association took effect in 1986 and trusteeship ended in 1990.

economy.description: External assistance, public services, fishing and agriculture support the economy of these widely dispersed islands.
economy.industries: tourism, construction; specialized aquaculture, craft items (shell and wood)
economy.exports: fish, diamonds, garments (2023)

partyFact.title: A national anthem edited from a poem
partyFact.text: Moldova’s anthem began as a twelve-verse poem about language. The official song selects verses 1, 2, 5, 9 and 12 rather than simply using the opening verses.

history.text: Much of present-day Moldova, then Bessarabia, passed from Ottoman-linked Moldavia to Russia in 1812. It united with Romania in 1918, was taken by the USSR in 1940, occupied by Romania in 1941–1944, and returned to Soviet rule until 1991.

economy.industries: sugar processing, vegetable oil, food processing, agricultural machinery; foundry equipment, refrigerators and freezers, washing machines; hosiery, shoes, textiles
economy.exports: insulated wire, garments, refined petroleum, seed oils, wheat (2023)

partyFact.title: A tiny country with its own anthem language
partyFact.text: Monaco’s official anthem lyrics are in Monegasque, not French. Its music was adopted in 1867, while the official words followed in 1931.

history.text: The Grimaldi family established rule in 1297, with interruptions. Monaco was annexed by France in 1793–1814 and under Sardinian protection in 1815–1861. A treaty recognised its sovereignty in 1861.

economy.industries: banking, insurance, tourism, construction, small-scale industrial and consumer products
economy.exports: jewelry, perfumes, watches, packaged medicines, cars (2021)

partyFact.title: A landscape that changes with climate cycles
partyFact.text: Dauria’s alternating wet and dry periods create shifting habitats of grassland, forest, lakes and wetlands. These support migratory birds and the cross-border movements of Mongolian gazelles.

history.text: Qing rule over Outer Mongolia developed from 1691 and ended with the independence declaration of 1911. Chinese forces reoccupied it in 1919–1921. Later Soviet influence was extensive, but Mongolia was not a Soviet republic.

economy.industries: construction and construction materials; mining (coal, copper, molybdenum, fluorspar, tin, tungsten, gold); oil; food and beverages; processing of animal products, cashmere and natural fiber manufacturing
economy.exports: coal, copper ore, gold, iron ore, crude petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: Glaciers above, rivers below
partyFact.text: Durmitor’s dramatic landscape was carved by glaciers, then cut by rivers and underground streams. The Tara canyon is among Europe’s deepest gorges.

history.text: Montenegro maintained varying degrees of autonomy while neighbouring territories were under Ottoman rule. Independence was internationally recognised in 1878. It joined the Yugoslav state in 1918 and restored separate independence in 2006.

economy.industries: steelmaking, aluminum, agricultural processing, consumer goods, tourism
economy.exports: electricity, aluminum, copper ore, aluminum ore, packaged medicine (2023)

partyFact.title: Two very different city plans side by side
partyFact.text: Rabat combines medieval walls and monuments with a large planned city built under the French protectorate. Its urban landscape lets you read two very different eras together.

history.text: Most of Morocco was a French protectorate from 1912 to 1956, with separate Spanish zones and an international zone at Tangier. Independence was restored in 1956; some territorial questions followed different timelines.

economy.industries: automotive parts, phosphate mining and processing, aerospace, food processing, leather goods, textiles, construction, energy, tourism
economy.exports: fertilizers, cars, garments, insulated wire, tomatoes (2023)

partyFact.title: Coral reefs and savannah in one protected landscape
partyFact.text: The Maputo–iSimangaliso coastal region crosses Mozambique and South Africa. Its habitats range from reefs and seagrass to freshwater lakes, mangroves and savannah.

history.text: Portuguese coastal footholds began around 1500, with inland colonial control expanding much later. Portuguese rule ended with independence in 1975.

economy.industries: aluminum, petroleum products, chemicals (fertilizer, soap, paints), textiles, cement, glass, asbestos, tobacco, food, beverages
economy.exports: coal, natural gas, aluminum, gold, precious stones (2023)

partyFact.title: A whole landscape of sacred architecture
partyFact.text: Bagan was a major imperial capital between the eleventh and thirteenth centuries. Its temples, stupas, monasteries and wall paintings preserve the scale of that Buddhist civilisation.

history.text: Britain conquered Burma in stages in 1824–1885 and annexed the remaining kingdom in 1886. Japanese occupation lasted 1942–1945. Independence from Britain came in 1948.

economy.industries: agricultural processing; wood and wood products; copper, tin, tungsten, iron; cement, construction materials; pharmaceuticals; fertilizer; oil and natural gas; garments; jade and gems
economy.exports: garments, natural gas, dried legumes, rare-earth metal compounds, precious stones (2023)

partyFact.title: A desert that drinks fog
partyFact.text: In the Namib Sand Sea, fog is the principal source of water. Animals adapted to it live among dunes made from material transported by rivers, ocean currents and wind.

history.text: Germany established South West Africa in 1884. South Africa occupied it in 1915 and later administered it under a mandate, continuing after that mandate was revoked. Namibia became independent in 1990.

economy.description: Mining, fishing, agriculture and tourism are important; diamonds and uranium are among the major exports.
economy.industries: mining, tourism, fishing, agriculture
economy.exports: gold, diamonds, radioactive chemicals, fish, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: An island with a distinctive language
partyFact.text: Nauru developed in considerable isolation because currents made landing difficult. Its language does not closely resemble those of neighbouring Pacific societies, according to the Factbook’s historical account.

history.text: Germany annexed Nauru in 1888. Australian-led administration began in 1914, later under international mandates and trusteeship. Japan occupied it in 1942–1945. Independence came in 1968.

economy.description: Fishing licences, external assistance, the Australian regional processing centre and remaining phosphate activities support income.
economy.industries: phosphate mining, offshore banking, coconut products
economy.exports: fish, phosphates (2023)

partyFact.title: Everest shares a home with red pandas
partyFact.text: Sagarmatha National Park is famous for Everest, but it also protects rare wildlife such as red pandas and snow leopards. Its habitats extend through valleys, forests and high mountain terrain.

history.text: Nepal was not formally colonised by a European power. The Anglo-Nepalese War of 1814–1816 ended with territorial losses and British influence; a 1923 treaty explicitly recognised Nepal’s independence.

economy.industries: tourism, carpets, textiles, small rice, jute, sugar, oilseed mills, cigarettes, cement and brick production
economy.exports: knotted carpets, garments, flat-rolled iron, synthetic fibers, palm oil (2023)

partyFact.title: Amsterdam’s canals were a city-building system
partyFact.text: The canal ring was a planned expansion onto drained marshland. Concentric waterways and the spaces between them created new neighbourhoods and became an influential model of urban planning.

history.text: Habsburg rule in the 1500s led to revolt against Spain from 1568. The northern provinces declared separation in 1581, recognised in 1648. French control lasted 1795–1813; Nazi occupation lasted 1940–1945.

economy.description: High-income, core EU- and eurozone-member economy.
economy.industries: agroindustries, metal and engineering products, electrical machinery and equipment, chemicals, petroleum, construction, microelectronics, fishing
economy.exports: refined petroleum, vaccines, machinery, crude petroleum, broadcasting equipment (2023)

partyFact.title: A parrot that lives in the mountains
partyFact.text: New Zealand’s kea is the world’s only alpine parrot. It lives in a landscape that also contains forests with trees more than 800 years old.

history.text: British sovereignty was asserted in 1840 following the Treaty of Waitangi, whose interpretation remains contested. Dominion status came in 1907; legislative autonomy followed in 1947. Māori communities experienced substantial dispossession during colonisation.

economy.description: High-income, globally integrated Pacific island economy.
economy.industries: agriculture, forestry, fishing, logs and wood articles, manufacturing, mining, construction, financial services, real estate services, tourism
economy.exports: milk, wood, beef, butter, sheep and goat meat (2023)

partyFact.title: A colonial town whose growth stopped
partyFact.text: León Viejo never developed into a modern city on the same site. That makes its ruins an unusually clear record of an early Spanish settlement’s layout and society.

history.text: Spanish conquest began in the 1520s. Independence from Spain came in 1821; Nicaragua left the Central American federation in 1838. US military occupations occurred in 1912–1925 and 1926–1933, while the Caribbean coast had a separate British-influenced history.

economy.industries: food processing, chemicals, machinery and metal products, knit and woven apparel, petroleum refining and distribution, beverages, footwear, wood, electric wire harness manufacturing, mining
economy.exports: garments, gold, insulated wire, coffee, beef (2023)

partyFact.title: A mountain refuge surrounded by the Sahara
partyFact.text: The volcanic Aïr massif forms a pocket of different climate, plants and animals within the Ténéré desert. The reserve protects that contrast between mountain refuge and vast desert.

history.text: French military conquest expanded around 1900 and Niger became a colony in 1922. Colonial rule ended with independence in 1960.

economy.industries: uranium mining, petroleum, cement, brick, soap, textiles, food processing, chemicals, slaughterhouses
economy.exports: gold, oil seeds, uranium and thorium ore, radioactive chemicals, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: A forest that is also an art landscape
partyFact.text: The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove contains shrines, sculptures and sanctuaries among its trees and river bends. It preserves a Yoruba tradition of sacred forests once widespread around settlements.

history.text: Britain annexed Lagos in 1861 and gradually expanded control. The northern and southern protectorates were amalgamated in 1914; Nigeria became independent in 1960.

economy.industries: crude oil, coal, tin, columbite; rubber products, wood; hides and skins, textiles, cement and other construction materials, food products, footwear, chemicals, fertilizer, printing, ceramics, steel
economy.exports: crude petroleum, natural gas, gold, fertilizers, cocoa beans (2023)

partyFact.title: Ancient daily life painted on tomb walls
partyFact.text: Some Koguryo tombs preserve murals showing a world that left few other remains. Painted tombs are rare among the thousands discovered across Korea and China.

history.text: Japan colonised Korea from 1910 to 1945. Soviet forces occupied the northern half in 1945–1948; North Korea was established as a separate state in 1948.

economy.description: One of the last centrally planned economies.
economy.industries: military products; machine building, electric power, chemicals; mining (coal, iron ore, limestone, magnesite, graphite, copper, zinc, lead, and precious metals), metallurgy; textiles, food processing; tourism
economy.exports: fake hair, iron alloys, tungsten ore, electricity, cars (2023)

partyFact.title: A lake with ancient survivors
partyFact.text: Lake Ohrid shelters freshwater species with very old evolutionary lineages. Around its shores, archaeological evidence also records prehistoric settlements built on piles over the water.

history.text: Ottoman rule covered the area from the late 1300s until 1912. It then came under Serbian rule and later Yugoslavia, with wartime occupations interrupting that period. Independence came in 1991.

economy.industries: food processing, beverages, textiles, chemicals, iron, steel, cement, energy, pharmaceuticals, automotive parts
economy.exports: reaction and catalytic products, insulated wire, electricity, garments, seats (2023)

partyFact.title: A cliff that continues under the sea
partyFact.text: The walls of Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord rise as much as 1,400 metres above the water and extend around 500 metres below sea level. The visible cliff is only part of the landscape.

history.text: Norway shared a crown with Denmark from 1380 until 1814, then with Sweden from 1814 to 1905. Nazi Germany occupied Norway from 1940 to 1945.

economy.description: High-income, non-EU economy with trade links via European Economic Area (EEA).
economy.industries: petroleum and gas, shipping, fishing, aquaculture, food processing, shipbuilding, pulp and paper products, metals, chemicals, timber, mining, textiles
economy.exports: natural gas, crude petroleum, fish, refined petroleum, aluminum (2023)

partyFact.title: A tree resin that powered trade routes
partyFact.text: Frankincense helped connect Oman’s trees, desert caravan stops and ports to the wider ancient world. The Land of Frankincense sites preserve several parts of that trading system.

history.text: Portugal controlled Muscat and other coastal strongholds in 1507–1650. Oman later became an imperial power itself. British influence was substantial, but Oman was not formally a British colony.

economy.industries: crude oil production and refining, natural and liquefied natural gas production; construction, cement, copper, steel, chemicals, optic fiber
economy.exports: crude petroleum, refined petroleum, natural gas, semi-finished iron, fertilizers (2023)

partyFact.title: A city remembered through its tombs
partyFact.text: Thatta was the capital of three successive dynasties before Mughal rule. Its elaborate Makli necropolis preserves the artistic traditions of centuries of Sindh’s history.

history.text: The territories of present-day Pakistan came under British control at different times: Sindh in 1843 and Punjab in 1849, with other areas following different arrangements. Pakistan became independent with the partition of British India in 1947.

economy.industries: textiles and apparel, food processing, pharmaceuticals, surgical instruments, construction materials, paper products, fertilizer, shrimp
economy.exports: garments, fabric, refined petroleum, rice, cotton fabric (2023)

partyFact.title: Seawater lakes cut off from the sea
partyFact.text: Palau’s Rock Islands have an exceptional concentration of marine lakes: seawater enclosed by land. Their isolation has supported distinctive populations and continuing species discoveries.

history.text: Spain controlled Palau in the late 1800s and sold it to Germany in 1899. Japan took control in 1914; US administration followed World War II under a UN trusteeship from 1947. Independence in free association with the US came in 1994.

economy.description: Tourism, external assistance and fishing support a small economy closely connected to the United States.
economy.industries: tourism, fishing, subsistence agriculture
economy.exports: ships, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: Sharing spring water by tradition
partyFact.text: Battir’s terraced gardens are fed by channels carrying water from underground sources. A traditional allocation system shares the collected water among village families.

history.text: Ottoman rule lasted 1516/1517–1917/1918, followed by British administration and the mandate until 1948. Jordan controlled the West Bank and Egypt administered Gaza in 1948–1967. Israel occupied both in 1967. Palestinian self-government began in the 1990s; occupation and sovereignty remain unresolved, with Gaza’s status after Israel’s 2005 withdrawal disputed by Israel and international bodies.

economy.description: Services, commerce, agriculture and manufacturing support livelihoods, alongside remittances and external assistance. Conflict and restrictions on movement severely disrupt the economy; conditions differ between the West Bank and Gaza.
economy.industries: Food processing, textiles, stone and construction materials, agriculture and local services.
economy.exports: Stone, agricultural products and manufactured goods are among the export activities described in the territorial profiles.
economy.snapshot: Structural overview; wartime conditions change rapidly.

partyFact.title: A natural bridge between continents
partyFact.text: Darién links the ecosystems of North and South America. Within one national park are beaches, mangroves, swamps and both lowland and upland tropical forests.

history.text: Spain colonised the isthmus from the early 1500s to 1821. Panama then joined Gran Colombia and remained linked to Colombia until 1903. The US administered the Canal Zone in 1903–1979; full control of the canal transferred in 1999.

economy.description: The canal, ports, logistics, commerce and finance make services central to Panama’s economy.
economy.industries: construction, brewing, cement and other construction materials, sugar milling
economy.exports: copper ore, ships, refined petroleum, bananas, fish (2023)

partyFact.title: Agriculture developed here independently
partyFact.text: At Kuk, people transformed highland wetlands into farmland over thousands of years. Archaeology points to an independent origin of agriculture, including early drainage ditches dug with wooden tools.

history.text: Germany and Britain divided eastern New Guinea in 1884. Australian administration developed from 1906 and expanded after Germany’s defeat in 1914, with Japanese occupation of parts during World War II. Papua New Guinea became independent in 1975.

economy.industries: oil and gas; mining (gold, copper, and nickel); palm oil processing; plywood and wood chip production; copra crushing; construction; tourism; fishing; livestock (pork, poultry, cattle) and dairy farming; spice products (turmeric, vanilla, ginger, cardamom, chili, pepper, citronella, and nutmeg)
economy.exports: natural gas, gold, copper ore, palm oil, nickel (2023)

partyFact.title: Ruins of a different kind of planned community
partyFact.text: The Jesuit missions at Trinidad and Jesús preserve more than churches. They are remains of settlements built around religious, social and economic projects in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

history.text: Spanish settlement began with Asunción in 1537. Paraguay became independent from Spain in 1811.

economy.industries: sugar processing, cement, textiles, beverages, wood products, steel, base metals, electric power
economy.exports: soybeans, beef, electricity, corn, soybean meal (2023)

partyFact.title: Tropical mountains with glaciers
partyFact.text: Peru’s Cordillera Blanca is the world’s highest tropical mountain range. Huascarán National Park combines glaciers and glacial lakes with wildlife such as spectacled bears and Andean condors.

history.text: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire began in 1532. Independence was declared in 1821 and secured through major military victories in 1824; the last mainland Spanish stronghold surrendered in 1826.

economy.industries: mining and refining of minerals; steel, metal fabrication; petroleum extraction and refining, natural gas and natural gas liquefaction; fishing and fish processing, cement, glass, textiles, clothing, food processing, beer, soft drinks, rubber, machinery, electrical machinery, chemicals, furniture
economy.exports: copper ore, gold, refined copper, refined petroleum, grapes (2023)

partyFact.title: A mountain with species of its own
partyFact.text: Mount Hamiguitan shelters plants and animals found nowhere else. Its elevation changes create different habitats within one mountain ridge, including homes for the Philippine eagle and cockatoo.

history.text: Spanish colonial rule developed from 1565 to 1898. US rule followed in 1898–1946, interrupted by Japanese occupation in 1942–1945. Full independence was recognised in 1946.

economy.description: Services, including business-process outsourcing, manufacturing and remittances are important sources of income.
economy.industries: semiconductors and electronics assembly, business process outsourcing, food and beverage manufacturing, construction, electric/gas/water supply, chemical products, radio/television/communications equipment and apparatus, petroleum and fuel, textile and garments, non-metallic minerals, basic metal industries, transport equipment
economy.exports: integrated circuits, machine parts, gold, insulated wire, semiconductors (2023)

partyFact.title: European bison have a forest stronghold
partyFact.text: Białowieża Forest, shared with Belarus, protects the largest population of European bison. Its old forest includes both broadleaf trees and conifers.

history.text: Partitions in 1772, 1793 and 1795 divided Poland among Russia, Prussia and Austria; it regained independence in 1918. Nazi Germany and the USSR invaded in 1939. German occupation ended in 1945, followed by a Soviet-dominated political order until 1989.

economy.industries: machine building, iron and steel, coal mining, chemicals, shipbuilding, food processing, glass, beverages, textiles
economy.exports: vehicle parts/accessories, electric batteries, plastic products, cars, seats (2023)

partyFact.title: An aqueduct built to outlast a siege
partyFact.text: Elvas’s defences include the Amoreira aqueduct, which helped supply the fortified town during long sieges. Its elaborate dry-ditch fortifications form an enormous interconnected defensive system.

history.text: Portugal became an independent kingdom in the 1100s and later a colonial power. It shared the Spanish monarch under the Iberian Union in 1580–1640. French invasions and occupation affected it in 1807–1811.

economy.industries: textiles, clothing, footwear, wood and cork, paper and pulp, chemicals, fuels and lubricants, automobiles and auto parts, base metals, minerals, porcelain and ceramics, glassware, technology, telecommunications; dairy products, wine, other foodstuffs; ship construction and refurbishment; tourism, plastics, financial services, optics
economy.exports: cars, garments, vehicle parts/accessories, unpackaged medicine, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: Before gas, there were pearls
partyFact.text: Al Zubarah prospered through pearl diving and trade in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Windblown desert sand later protected the abandoned town’s streets, homes and harbour remains.

history.text: Ottoman forces were present from 1871 to 1915. Qatar became a British protectorate in 1916 and gained independence in 1971, with the local ruling dynasty continuing.

economy.industries: liquefied natural gas, crude oil production and refining, ammonia, fertilizer, petrochemicals, steel reinforcing bars, cement, commercial ship repair
economy.exports: natural gas, crude petroleum, refined petroleum, plastics, fertilizers (2023)

partyFact.title: Where forest slowly reclaimed savannah
partyFact.text: Odzala-Kokoua records forest returning to savannah after the ice ages. Forests of different ages meet there, helping explain the park’s exceptional variety of primates and other wildlife.

history.text: France established colonial control through treaties and expansion from 1880. The territory became part of French Equatorial Africa and gained independence as the Republic of the Congo in 1960.

economy.description: Primarily an oil- and natural resources-based economy.
economy.industries: petroleum extraction, cement, lumber, brewing, sugar, palm oil, soap, flour, cigarettes
economy.exports: crude petroleum, refined copper, gold, wood, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: Rome’s province beyond the Danube
partyFact.text: Dacia was the Roman Empire’s only province entirely north of the Danube. Its frontier in today’s Romania operated from 106 to 271 CE and left forts, watchtowers and ramparts.

history.text: Wallachia and Moldavia were under varying Ottoman suzerainty for centuries; they united in 1859. Independence was proclaimed in 1877 and recognised in 1878. Transylvania had a different Habsburg and Hungarian history before joining Romania in 1918.

economy.industries: electric machinery and equipment, auto assembly, textiles and footwear, light machinery, metallurgy, chemicals, food processing, petroleum refining, mining, timber, construction materials
economy.exports: cars, vehicle parts/accessories, insulated wire, garments, wheat (2023)

partyFact.title: An Arctic island the ice sheets missed
partyFact.text: Wrangel Island was not covered by glaciers during the Quaternary Ice Age. That history helped it retain unusually rich Arctic biodiversity, including hundreds of plant species.

history.text: Medieval Rus’ principalities came under Mongol conquest in the 1230s–1240s and paid tribute to the Golden Horde. Moscow’s final break with that domination is conventionally dated to 1480. Russia later became an imperial power itself.

economy.industries: complete range of mining and extractive industries producing coal, oil, gas, chemicals, and metals; all forms of machine building from rolling mills to high-performance aircraft and space vehicles; defense industries (including radar, missile production, advanced electronic components), shipbuilding; road and rail transportation equipment; communications equipment; agricultural machinery, tractors, and construction equipment; electric power generating and transmitting equipment; medical and scientific instruments; consumer durables, textiles, foodstuffs, handicrafts
economy.exports: crude petroleum, refined petroleum, natural gas, coal, fertilizers (2023)

partyFact.title: A rainforest with peat bogs and moors
partyFact.text: Nyungwe is more than a forest of tall trees: it also includes peat bogs, grasslands and moorland. This mix helps support hundreds of bird species and rare mammals.

history.text: Germany established colonial control in the 1890s. Belgium occupied Rwanda in 1916 and later administered it under mandate and trusteeship until independence in 1962.

economy.industries: cement, agricultural products, small-scale beverages, soap, furniture, shoes, plastic goods, textiles, cigarettes
economy.exports: gold, rare earth ores, coffee, tea, tin ores (2023)

partyFact.title: A Caribbean fortress with a human story
partyFact.text: Brimstone Hill’s imposing defences were designed by the British and built through the labour of enslaved Africans. The surviving fortress records both military engineering and the people forced to construct it.

history.text: English and French settlers divided Saint Kitts during the 1600s. Britain obtained full control in 1713. British rule over the federation ended with independence in 1983.

economy.industries: tourism, cotton, salt, copra, clothing, footwear, beverages
economy.exports: ships, measuring instruments, beer, electrical transformers, electrical control boards (2023)

partyFact.title: Twin peaks above a hidden reef world
partyFact.text: Saint Lucia’s Pitons rise dramatically above the sea, but the protected area continues underwater. Coral reefs occupy almost 60% of its marine portion.

history.text: France and Britain repeatedly contested Saint Lucia in the 1600s–1700s. Britain finally secured it in 1814 and ruled until independence in 1979.

economy.description: Upper middle-income, tourism-based Caribbean island economy.
economy.industries: tourism; clothing, assembly of electronic components, beverages, corrugated cardboard boxes, lime processing, coconut processing
economy.exports: refined petroleum, gravel and crushed stone, beer, liquor, paper containers (2023)

partyFact.title: A garden older than many modern countries
partyFact.text: Saint Vincent’s Botanic Gardens was founded in 1765. It began as a centre for studying and exchanging medicinal plants and became an important conservation and research site.

history.text: French settlement began in 1719 after prolonged Indigenous resistance. Britain obtained the island in 1763; France retook it in 1779, and Britain regained it in 1783. Independence came in 1979.

economy.industries: tourism; food processing, cement, furniture, clothing, starch
economy.exports: ships, wheat flours, animal food, shellfish, construction vehicles (2023)

partyFact.title: The country that skipped a Friday
partyFact.text: Samoa went straight from 29 to 31 December in 2011 when it changed sides of the International Date Line. Friday, 30 December never occurred there that year.

history.text: Germany ruled western Samoa from 1900 to 1914. New Zealand then occupied and administered it, later under mandate and trusteeship, until independence in 1962. American Samoa followed a separate history.

economy.description: A Pacific island economy supported by agriculture, fishing, services and remittances.
economy.industries: food processing, building materials, auto parts
economy.exports: refined petroleum, integrated circuits, coconut oil, fish, insulated wire (2023)

partyFact.title: A medieval republic that kept going
partyFact.text: San Marino’s historic centre preserves the institutions of a free republic dating from the Middle Ages. Its government still operates within a cityscape shaped by Mount Titano.

history.text: San Marino preserved a long tradition of independent republican government rather than a sustained colonial period. Brief occupations included Cesare Borgia in 1503 and Cardinal Alberoni in 1739; German and Allied forces entered during fighting in 1944.

economy.industries: tourism, banking, textiles, electronics, ceramics, cement, wine
economy.exports: washing and bottling machines, other foods, packaged medicine, woodworking machines, aircraft (2023)

partyFact.title: An oasis with millions of palms
partyFact.text: Al-Ahsa contains about 2.5 million date palms. Its canals, springs, wells and gardens show how generations built a settled landscape in an arid region.

history.text: Parts of today’s Saudi Arabia, particularly the Hejaz, were under Ottoman rule from 1517 to 1916, with interruptions and varying control. The modern kingdom was unified in 1932; the entire present territory was never one European colony.

economy.industries: crude oil production, petroleum refining, basic petrochemicals, ammonia, industrial gases, sodium hydroxide (caustic soda), cement, fertilizer, plastics, metals, commercial ship repair, commercial aircraft repair, construction
economy.exports: crude petroleum, refined petroleum, plastics, alcohols, ships (2023)

partyFact.title: An antelope on a giant scale
partyFact.text: Niokolo-Koba shelters the giant eland, among the largest antelopes. Its river-fed forests and savannahs also create habitats for chimpanzees and many other animals.

history.text: France established a settlement at Saint-Louis in 1659 and later expanded colonial control inland. Senegal became independent in 1960, initially as part of the short-lived Mali Federation.

economy.description: Lower middle-income, services-driven West African economy.
economy.industries: agricultural and fish processing, phosphate mining, fertilizer production, petroleum refining, zircon, and gold mining, construction materials, ship construction and repair
economy.exports: gold, refined petroleum, phosphoric acid, fish, cement (2023)

partyFact.title: Serbia’s capital before Belgrade
partyFact.text: Stari Ras was an early Serbian capital. Its surrounding churches, monasteries and fortifications preserve connections between the medieval Byzantine and western European worlds.

history.text: Ottoman conquest culminated in the fall of the Serbian despotate in 1459. Autonomy developed after nineteenth-century uprisings; independence was internationally recognised in 1878. Serbia later formed part of Yugoslavia and became a separate state in 2006.

economy.industries: automobiles, base metals, furniture, food processing, machinery, chemicals, sugar, tires, clothes, pharmaceuticals
economy.exports: insulated wire, electricity, copper ore, plastic products, electric motors (2023)

partyFact.title: A giant-tortoise stronghold
partyFact.text: Remote Aldabra supports an extraordinary population of giant tortoises. Its four main coral islands surround a lagoon, and difficult access has helped limit human disturbance.

history.text: France claimed the Seychelles in 1756 and settlement began in 1770. Britain took control during the Napoleonic era, formalised in 1814. Independence came in 1976.

economy.industries: fishing, tourism, beverages
economy.exports: fish, scrap iron, animal meal, broadcasting equipment, ships (2023)

partyFact.title: A rainforest home for small hippos
partyFact.text: The Gola-Tiwai landscape shelters pygmy hippopotamuses as well as forest elephants. It also supports more than a thousand plant species and hundreds of bird species.

history.text: British-sponsored settlement at Freetown began in 1787. The coastal colony was established in 1808 and an inland protectorate in 1896. Both became independent as Sierra Leone in 1961.

economy.industries: diamond mining; iron ore, rutile and bauxite mining; small-scale manufacturing (beverages, textiles, footwear)
economy.exports: iron ore, titanium ore, diamonds, aluminum ore, cocoa beans (2023)

partyFact.title: A garden that helped change an industry
partyFact.text: Singapore Botanic Gardens became a major centre for rubber cultivation research. A garden in the city helped shape plantation agriculture across Southeast Asia.

history.text: A British trading settlement began in 1819; Singapore became a crown colony in 1867. Japanese occupation lasted 1942–1945. It gained self-government in 1959, joined Malaysia in 1963 and became independent in 1965.

economy.description: Trade, logistics, finance and other business services combine with advanced manufacturing in a highly connected economy.
economy.industries: electronics, chemicals, financial services, oil drilling equipment, petroleum refining, biomedical products, scientific instruments, telecommunication equipment, processed food and beverages, ship repair, offshore platform construction, entrepot trade
economy.exports: integrated circuits, refined petroleum, machinery, vaccines, gold (2023)

partyFact.title: Different traditions, one building material
partyFact.text: Eight listed Carpathian churches show how Catholic, Protestant and eastern Christian communities expressed their architecture in wood. Their designs adapted to local conditions and different worship practices.

history.text: Most Slovak territory formed part of the Kingdom of Hungary for centuries, later within the Habsburg monarchy until 1918. A German-aligned Slovak state existed in 1939–1945, with German occupation from 1944. Slovakia became separate from Czechoslovakia in 1993.

economy.industries: automobiles; metal and metal products; electricity, gas, coke, oil, nuclear fuel; chemicals, synthetic fibers, wood and paper products; machinery; earthenware and ceramics; textiles; electrical and optical apparatus; rubber products; food and beverages; pharmaceutical
economy.exports: cars, vehicle parts/accessories, video displays, broadcasting equipment, refined petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: Waterfalls inside the Earth
partyFact.text: Škocjan’s limestone cave system contains underground waterfalls and around six kilometres of passages. The surrounding Kras region helped give the term “karst” to this type of landscape.

history.text: Slovene lands were largely within Habsburg domains for centuries until 1918, with a French interruption in parts in 1809–1813. Axis powers divided and occupied the territory in 1941–1945. Slovenia left Yugoslavia in 1991.

economy.industries: ferrous metallurgy and aluminum products, lead and zinc smelting; electronics (including military electronics), trucks, automobiles, electric power equipment, wood products, textiles, chemicals, machine tools
economy.exports: packaged medicine, cars, refined petroleum, vehicle parts/accessories, plastic products (2023)

partyFact.title: A coral lagoon that became a lake
partyFact.text: Lake Tegano on Rennell Island was once an atoll lagoon. The island’s uplift left a large brackish lake surrounded by limestone and forest.

history.text: Britain established a protectorate over the southern islands in 1893, with further islands added later. Japan occupied parts in 1942–1945. Independence came in 1978.

economy.industries: fish (tuna), mining, timber
economy.exports: wood, fish, gold, precious metal ore, palm oil (2023)

partyFact.title: A painted cattle gallery in the rocks
partyFact.text: The Laas Geel rock shelters near Hargeisa, in Somaliland, preserve vivid prehistoric cattle paintings. The artwork records a pastoral world thousands of years before modern borders.

history.text: British and Italian colonial rule developed in the late 1800s in different parts of present-day Somalia. British Somaliland and the Italian-administered UN trust territory became independent and united in 1960; French Somaliland later became Djibouti separately.

economy.description: Livestock, agriculture, trade and telecommunications support livelihoods, alongside substantial remittances and external assistance.
economy.industries: light industries, including sugar refining, textiles, wireless communication
economy.exports: sheep and goats, gold, postage stamps/documents, other animals, cattle (2023)

partyFact.title: A scar from two billion years ago
partyFact.text: Vredefort preserves part of a vast meteorite impact structure formed about 2.02 billion years ago. Erosion has exposed a deep cross-section of that ancient collision.

history.text: Dutch settlement at the Cape began in 1652. British control developed from 1795 and permanently from 1806, expanding after wars with African kingdoms and Boer republics. The Union formed in 1910; legislative independence followed in 1931. Apartheid ended with democratic elections in 1994.

economy.industries: mining (world's largest producer of platinum, gold, chromium), automobile assembly, metalworking, machinery, textiles, iron and steel, chemicals, fertilizer, foodstuffs, commercial ship repair
economy.exports: gold, platinum, coal, cars, iron ore (2023)

partyFact.title: Volcanoes made an underground tunnel network
partyFact.text: Jeju’s lava tubes preserve passages once occupied by flowing lava. The island also has a volcanic crater lake on Mount Halla and a dramatic tuff cone rising beside the sea.

history.text: Japan colonised Korea from 1910 to 1945. A US military government administered the southern half in 1945–1948; the Republic of Korea was established in 1948.

economy.description: High-income, export- and technology-oriented East Asian economy.
economy.industries: electronics, telecommunications, automobile production, chemicals, shipbuilding, steel
economy.exports: integrated circuits, cars, refined petroleum, plastics, machine parts (2023)

partyFact.title: Millions of animals on the move
partyFact.text: South Sudan’s Boma–Badingilo landscape supports a vast migration of antelopes. Seasonal rainfall and flooding drive animals between connected grasslands, wetlands and savannahs.

history.text: The south was incorporated into the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan condominium from 1899 to 1956, following earlier Egyptian expansion. It then formed part of independent Sudan until South Sudan became independent in 2011.

economy.description: Oil is central to export earnings and public finance. Agriculture, livestock and assistance support many households.
economy.industries: Oil production and agriculture; household livelihoods also depend on livestock, trade and external assistance.
economy.exports: crude petroleum, refined petroleum, forage crops, gold, scrap iron (2023)

partyFact.title: Spain’s highest peak is off Africa
partyFact.text: Teide stands on Tenerife in the Canary Islands. The volcanic structure rises roughly 7,500 metres from the ocean floor, much farther than the summit’s height above sea level suggests.

history.text: Roman rule covered much of the peninsula in antiquity. Muslim-ruled states controlled varying areas from 711 to 1492, alongside expanding Christian kingdoms. Napoleonic French occupation affected Spain in 1808–1814; modern Spain was itself a colonial power.

economy.industries: textiles and apparel (including footwear), food and beverages, metals and metal manufactures, chemicals, shipbuilding, automobiles, machine tools, tourism, clay and refractory products, footwear, pharmaceuticals, medical equipment
economy.exports: cars, packaged medicine, refined petroleum, vehicle parts/accessories, garments (2023)

partyFact.title: Paintings across a cave monastery
partyFact.text: Dambulla’s five cave sanctuaries contain 157 statues and roughly 2,100 square metres of Buddhist murals. The site has been a place of pilgrimage for more than two millennia.

history.text: Portugal controlled coastal areas from the 1500s until displacement by the Dutch in 1658. Britain took Dutch territories in 1796 and conquered the Kandyan kingdom in 1815. British rule ended with independence in 1948.

economy.description: Economic contraction in 2022-23 marked by increased poverty and significant inflation.
economy.industries: processing of rubber, tea, coconuts, tobacco and other agricultural commodities; tourism; clothing and textiles; mining
economy.exports: garments, tea, precious stones, used rubber tires, rubber products (2023)

partyFact.title: Dugongs off the desert coast
partyFact.text: Sudan’s Dungonab Bay supports a significant dugong population. Along this Red Sea coast, mangroves, seagrass beds and coral reefs create a very different world from the desert inland.

history.text: Turco-Egyptian conquest began in 1820–1821, followed by the independent Mahdist state in 1885–1898. Anglo-Egyptian condominium rule lasted from 1899 until independence in 1956.

economy.description: Agriculture, livestock, gold and services are important economic activities. Conflict has severely disrupted production, trade and livelihoods.
economy.industries: oil, cotton ginning, textiles, cement, edible oils, sugar, soap distilling, shoes, petroleum refining, pharmaceuticals, armaments, automobile/light truck assembly, milling
economy.exports: crude petroleum, gold, oil seeds, sheep and goats, ground nuts (2023)

partyFact.title: Dutch-speaking South America
partyFact.text: Dutch is Suriname’s official language, while Sranan Tongo is widely used as a common language. The country’s linguistic mix connects South America with the Netherlands, Africa and Asia.

history.text: English colonisation developed in the 1600s; the Dutch took control in 1667. British occupations interrupted Dutch rule in 1799–1802 and 1804–1816. Suriname became independent from the Netherlands in 1975.

economy.industries: gold mining, oil, lumber, food processing, fishing
economy.exports: gold, fish, refined petroleum, wood, tobacco (2023)

partyFact.title: A coastline still rising out of the sea
partyFact.text: Sweden’s High Coast is rebounding after the weight of ice-age glaciers was removed. Along the shared High Coast–Kvarken landscape, land rises, islands join and bays can become lakes.

history.text: Sweden belonged to the Kalmar Union from 1397, with repeated interruptions and contests over Danish-led rule, until 1523. It subsequently became a regional imperial power and was not a modern overseas colony.

economy.industries: iron and steel, precision equipment (bearings, radio and telephone parts, armaments), wood pulp and paper products, processed foods, motor vehicles
economy.exports: cars, refined petroleum, packaged medicine, paper, vehicle parts/accessories (2023)

partyFact.title: Retreating ice reveals a living experiment
partyFact.text: In the Jungfrau-Aletsch landscape, retreating glaciers expose fresh ground. Scientists can study the sequence in which plants colonise it, alongside the geological story of the Alps.

history.text: The Swiss Confederation developed from the late 1200s and gradually escaped Habsburg and imperial authority. Independence from the Holy Roman Empire was formally recognised in 1648. French invasion imposed the Helvetic Republic in 1798–1803.

economy.industries: machinery, chemicals, watches, textiles, precision instruments, tourism, banking, insurance, pharmaceuticals
economy.exports: gold, packaged medicine, vaccines, nitrogen compounds, base metal watches (2023)

partyFact.title: Whole villages from late antiquity
partyFact.text: Northern Syria’s listed ancient villages preserve homes, baths, cisterns and religious buildings. Their layouts reveal rural life and agricultural engineering many centuries before modern towns.

history.text: Ottoman rule lasted from 1516 until 1918. France established control in 1920 and governed under a mandate. Independence developed during World War II; the last French troops left in 1946.

economy.industries: petroleum, textiles, food processing, beverages, tobacco, phosphate rock mining, cement, oil seeds crushing, automobile assembly
economy.exports: olive oil, phosphates, spice seeds, cotton, tomatoes (2023)

partyFact.title: Plantations organised like miniature towns
partyFact.text: The roças combined fields, processing machinery, housing and social facilities in planned complexes. They reveal how coffee and cocoa production shaped island life, including the coercion of colonial labour.

history.text: Portuguese settlement of the previously uninhabited islands began in the late 1400s. The plantation colony became independent in 1975.

economy.description: Lower middle-income Central African island economy.
economy.industries: light construction, textiles, soap, beer, fish processing, timber
economy.exports: crude petroleum, cocoa beans, vehicle parts/accessories, palm oil, aircraft parts (2023)

partyFact.title: A forest fed by rivers in dry country
partyFact.text: Tigrovaya Balka protects rare tugay floodplain forests. Asiatic poplars survive here in a river-fed ecosystem surrounded by desert and mountain landscapes.

history.text: Russian conquest brought parts of the territory under direct rule in the late 1800s; other areas belonged to the Russian-protected Emirate of Bukhara. Soviet control followed in the 1920s. Tajikistan became a union republic in 1929 and independent in 1991.

economy.industries: aluminum, cement, coal, gold, silver, antimony, textile, vegetable oil
economy.exports: gold, precious metal ore, aluminum, lead ore, antimony (2023)

partyFact.title: Footprints older than our species
partyFact.text: The Ngorongoro area preserves evidence of early human relatives, including footprints about 3.6 million years old. Its story reaches far beyond the wildlife visible there today.

history.text: Germany controlled mainland Tanganyika from the 1880s until World War I; British administration followed until independence in 1961. Zanzibar was an Omani-linked sultanate and British protectorate in 1890–1963. The two united in 1964.

economy.description: Emerging lower middle-income East African economy.
economy.industries: agricultural processing (sugar, beer, cigarettes, sisal twine); mining (diamonds, gold, and iron), salt, soda ash; cement, oil refining, shoes, apparel, wood products, fertilizer
economy.exports: gold, refined petroleum, dried legumes, refined copper, coal (2023)

partyFact.title: Stones that mark sacred space
partyFact.text: At Phu Phrabat, stone boundary markers and modified rock shelters turned a natural landscape into a Buddhist religious centre. Rock paintings also record occupation stretching back more than two millennia.

history.text: Thailand was never formally colonised by a European power. It negotiated concessions and lost territories while retaining sovereignty. Japan invaded in December 1941, then maintained troops under an alliance arrangement until 1945.

economy.industries: tourism, textiles and garments, agricultural processing, beverages, tobacco, cement, light manufacturing such as jewelry and electric appliances, computers and parts, integrated circuits, furniture, plastics, automobiles and automotive parts, agricultural machinery, air conditioning and refrigeration, ceramics, aluminum, chemical, environmental management, glass, granite and marble, leather, machinery and metal work, petrochemical, petroleum refining, pharmaceuticals, printing, pulp and paper, rubber, sugar, rice, fishing, cassava, world's second-largest tungsten producer and third-largest tin producer
economy.exports: machine parts, integrated circuits, trucks, cars, broadcasting equipment (2023)

partyFact.title: An island explained by a crocodile
partyFact.text: In a Timorese creation legend, a crocodile repays a boy’s kindness and ultimately becomes the island of Timor. Crocodiles are consequently addressed as “Grandfather” in this tradition.

history.text: Portuguese colonial influence began in the 1500s. Japan occupied the territory in 1942–1945. After a brief independence declaration in 1975, Indonesia invaded and occupied it until 1999. UN transitional administration lasted 1999–2002, when independence was restored.

economy.industries: printing, soap manufacturing, handicrafts, woven cloth
economy.exports: crude petroleum, natural gas, coffee, scrap iron, telephones (2023)

partyFact.title: Homes shaped like small towers
partyFact.text: The Batammariba of Koutammakou build remarkable earthen tower-houses. The architecture is tied to social life and a landscape of farmland, sacred rocks, springs and ceremonial places.

history.text: Germany established Togoland in 1884 and lost control in 1914. Britain and France administered separate mandates. French Togoland became independent as Togo in 1960; British Togoland joined what became Ghana in 1957.

economy.industries: phosphate mining, agricultural processing, cement, handicrafts, textiles, beverages
economy.exports: gold, refined petroleum, soybeans, phosphates, coconuts/brazil nuts/cashews (2023)

partyFact.title: A small island kingdom with a far-reaching past
partyFact.text: By around 1200, Tonga’s rulers had extended influence far across Polynesia and into parts of Melanesia and Micronesia. The modern kingdom is much smaller than that old network of influence.

history.text: Tonga retained its indigenous monarchy and was not formally annexed as a colony. It was a British protected state from 1900 to 1970, when full control of external affairs returned.

economy.industries: tourism, construction, fishing
economy.exports: refined petroleum, gold, processed fruits and nuts, cassava, fish (2023)

partyFact.title: Music made from oil drums
partyFact.text: Trinidad and Tobago’s steelpan grew out of experiments with metal containers and discarded oil drums. Careful shaping and tuning turned an industrial object into a melodic instrument.

history.text: Spain colonised Trinidad from the late 1500s; Britain captured it in 1797. Tobago changed European rulers repeatedly before becoming British definitively in 1814. The islands were united administratively in 1889 and became independent in 1962.

economy.industries: petroleum and petroleum products, liquefied natural gas, methanol, ammonia, urea, steel products, beverages, food processing, cement, cotton textiles
economy.exports: natural gas, alcohols, ammonia, crude petroleum, iron reductions (2023)

partyFact.title: A Punic city without a Roman rebuild
partyFact.text: Kerkuane was abandoned around the time of the First Punic War. Because the Romans did not rebuild it, the surviving plan offers a rare view of a Phoenician-Punic town.

history.text: Ottoman rule began in 1574, later with substantial autonomy under local beys. France imposed a protectorate in 1881, which ended with independence in 1956.

economy.industries: petroleum, mining (particularly phosphate, iron ore), tourism, textiles, footwear, agribusiness, beverages
economy.exports: garments, insulated wire, olive oil, refined petroleum, crude petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: Four thousand years in an oasis
partyFact.text: Ancient Merv is a succession of cities within one Silk Road oasis. Its extensive remains record about 4,000 years of human history.

history.text: Russian conquest in the 1880s incorporated most of the territory into the empire. Soviet rule followed; Turkmenistan became a union republic in 1924 and independent in 1991.

economy.industries: natural gas, oil, petroleum products, textiles, food processing
economy.exports: natural gas, refined petroleum, fertilizers, crude petroleum, electricity (2023)

partyFact.title: An internet address that earns money
partyFact.text: The “.tv” internet domain belongs to Tuvalu. Licensing the domain provides income for a tiny Pacific country whose online address is recognised far beyond its islands.

history.text: The Ellice Islands became a British protectorate in 1892 and part of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands colony in 1916. They separated as Tuvalu in 1975–1976 and became independent in 1978.

economy.description: Fishing-access fees, foreign assistance, trust-fund income and licensing the .tv internet domain support public finances and livelihoods.
economy.industries: Fishing, small-scale food production and public services.
economy.exports: fish (2023)

partyFact.title: A city linked to the beginnings of coinage
partyFact.text: Sardis was the capital of wealthy Lydia, known for early coin production. Nearby Bin Tepe contains some of the world’s largest ancient burial mounds.

history.text: Modern Türkiye emerged from the Ottoman Empire, itself a major imperial power. Allied occupation affected parts of the former empire in 1918–1923, including Istanbul; the republic was proclaimed in 1923 after the independence war.

economy.industries: textiles, food processing, automobiles, electronics, mining (coal, chromate, copper, boron), steel, petroleum, construction, lumber, paper
economy.exports: garments, cars, gold, refined petroleum, vehicle parts/accessories (2023)

partyFact.title: An alpine world near the equator
partyFact.text: The Rwenzori Mountains have high-altitude landscapes with lakes, waterfalls and giant heather. Mount Margherita rises above 5,000 metres, creating a very different Uganda from the lowlands.

history.text: Britain declared the Uganda Protectorate in 1894, expanding its boundaries over subsequent years. Protectorate rule ended with independence in 1962.

economy.description: Low-income, primarily agrarian East African economy.
economy.industries: sugar processing, brewing, tobacco, cotton textiles; cement, steel production
economy.exports: gold, coffee, fish, refined petroleum, tobacco (2023)

partyFact.title: A cathedral imagined as a new Constantinople
partyFact.text: Kyiv’s Saint-Sophia Cathedral was designed to rival Hagia Sophia. It expressed the ambitions of an eleventh-century capital through architecture and religious art.

history.text: Different Ukrainian regions experienced Polish–Lithuanian, Russian, Habsburg and other rule. Most became part of the USSR in 1922; Nazi occupation affected the territory in 1941–1944. Independence came in 1991. Russia has occupied Crimea and parts of the east since 2014 and launched a full-scale invasion in 2022; those territories remain internationally recognised as Ukrainian.

economy.industries: industrial machinery, ferrous and nonferrous metals, automotive and aircraft components, electronics, chemicals, textiles, mining, construction
economy.exports: corn, seed oils, wheat, iron ore, soybeans (2023)

partyFact.title: Desert irrigation with Iron Age roots
partyFact.text: At Al Ain’s Hili sites, evidence survives of early aflaj irrigation. These engineered water channels helped sustain settled life in a desert landscape thousands of years ago.

history.text: The Trucial States entered maritime treaties with Britain from 1820 and exclusive protection agreements in 1892. The protected relationship ended in 1971, when the UAE formed; Ras Al Khaimah joined in 1972.

economy.industries: petroleum and petrochemicals; fishing, aluminum, cement, fertilizer, commercial ship repair, construction materials, handicrafts, textiles
economy.exports: crude petroleum, refined petroleum, gold, broadcasting equipment, natural gas (2023)

partyFact.title: A penguin with a knighthood
partyFact.text: Edinburgh Zoo is home to a king penguin called Major General Sir Nils Olav. The zoo identifies him as the world’s only knighted penguin—an unusually distinguished resident of a penguin enclosure.

history.text: The modern UK formed through unions of kingdoms and became a major colonial power. Earlier foreign conquests affected its constituent territories: Rome ruled much of Britain in 43–410 CE, and the Norman conquest of England began in 1066. The whole modern UK was not a later overseas colony.

economy.industries: machine tools, electric power equipment, automation equipment, railroad equipment, shipbuilding, aircraft, motor vehicles and parts, electronics and communications equipment, metals, chemicals, coal, petroleum, paper and paper products, food processing, textiles, clothing, other consumer goods
economy.exports: cars, gold, gas turbines, packaged medicine, crude petroleum (2023)

partyFact.title: Hundreds of miles beneath Kentucky
partyFact.text: Kentucky’s Mammoth Cave is the world’s longest known cave system, with hundreds of miles of mapped passages. Explorers have repeatedly connected neighbouring systems, revealing an even larger underground network.

history.text: European powers colonised different regions from the 1500s onward. The thirteen British colonies declared independence in 1776, recognised in 1783. Later US expansion incorporated territories with distinct Indigenous, Spanish, French, Mexican and other histories.

economy.description: Services dominate the economy, with major roles for finance, healthcare, technology and professional services, alongside manufacturing and energy.
economy.industries: highly diversified, world leading, high-technology innovator, second-largest industrial output in the world; petroleum, steel, motor vehicles, aerospace, telecommunications, chemicals, electronics, food processing, consumer goods, lumber, mining
economy.exports: crude petroleum, refined petroleum, natural gas, gas turbines, cars (2023)

partyFact.title: A town that helped feed distant continents
partyFact.text: Fray Bentos processed cattle from nearby grasslands into meat extract and corned beef for export to Europe. The surviving industrial landscape shows the whole chain from processing to shipment.

history.text: Spain and Portugal contested the region from the colonial era. Portuguese forces invaded in 1816, followed by incorporation into Brazil in 1822. Uruguay’s independence was recognised in 1828 after war and diplomacy.

economy.industries: food processing, electrical machinery, transportation equipment, petroleum products, textiles, chemicals, beverages
economy.exports: wood pulp, beef, milk, rice, wood (2023)

partyFact.title: A Silk Road city with an observatory
partyFact.text: Samarkand’s famous monuments include Ulugh Beg’s observatory as well as mosques and madrasas. Scholarship and astronomy were part of the city’s cultural world, alongside trade.

history.text: Russian imperial conquest brought much of the region under control in the 1860s–1870s, while Bukhara and Khiva became protectorates. Soviet rule followed in the 1920s; Uzbekistan was a union republic from 1924 until independence in 1991.

economy.industries: textiles, food processing, machine building, metallurgy, mining, hydrocarbon extraction, chemicals
economy.exports: gold, cotton yarn, garments, fertilizers, fabric (2023)

partyFact.title: Oral history meets archaeology
partyFact.text: Sites associated with Chief Roi Mata preserve places linked to his life, death and burial. Archaeological evidence and living oral traditions tell connected versions of this Vanuatu history.

history.text: France and Britain jointly administered the New Hebrides as a condominium from 1906. This unusual dual colonial system ended with independence as Vanuatu in 1980.

economy.industries: food and fish freezing, wood processing, meat canning
economy.exports: fish, ships, perfume plants, wood, copra (2023)

partyFact.title: A whole country on the heritage list
partyFact.text: Vatican City itself is a UNESCO World Heritage property. Within this tiny state are palaces, gardens, St Peter’s Basilica and works associated with artists including Michelangelo and Bernini.

history.text: The modern Vatican City State was created by the Lateran Treaty in 1929. Earlier papal territories were absorbed into Italy, with Rome taken in 1870. Vatican City’s history is therefore different from a conventional colony gaining independence.

economy.description: Tourism and museum admissions, donations, investments and sales of stamps and publications support Vatican activities. Vatican City and the Holy See have distinct but related finances.
economy.industries: printing; production of coins, medals, postage stamps; mosaics, staff uniforms; worldwide banking and financial activities

partyFact.title: Mountains shaped like giant tables
partyFact.text: Canaima’s tepuis are steep-sided, flat-topped mountains. Their cliffs and waterfalls, including Angel Falls, create a landscape very different from the pointed peaks people usually imagine.

history.text: Spanish colonisation began in the early 1500s. Independence was declared in 1811 and secured through the independence wars; Venezuela became a separate state from Gran Colombia in 1830.

economy.industries: agricultural products, livestock, raw materials, machinery and equipment, transport equipment, construction materials, medical equipment, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, iron and steel products, crude oil and petroleum products
economy.exports: crude petroleum, petroleum coke, scrap iron, alcohols, fertilizers (2023)

partyFact.title: Rivers that disappear underground
partyFact.text: The Phong Nha-Ke Bang–Hin Nam No karst landscape spans Vietnam and Laos. Hundreds of kilometres of caves and underground waterways have been documented in this ancient limestone terrain.

history.text: French conquest began in 1858 and control over Vietnam was consolidated in the 1880s. Japanese occupation and influence lasted 1940–1945. Independence was declared in 1945; French rule ended after war in 1954. The country was divided until reunification in 1976.

economy.description: Lower middle-income socialist East Asian economy.
economy.industries: food processing, garments, shoes, machine-building; mining, coal, steel; cement, chemical fertilizer, glass, tires, oil, mobile phones
economy.exports: broadcasting equipment, garments, integrated circuits, machine parts, footwear (2023)

partyFact.title: An island group full of local originals
partyFact.text: A large share of Socotra’s plants and reptiles occur nowhere else. UNESCO records endemism in about 37% of its plant species and 90% of its reptile species.

history.text: Northern Yemen experienced Ottoman rule in two periods, principally 1538–1635 and 1849–1918. Britain controlled Aden from 1839 and later protected surrounding southern territories until 1967. North and South Yemen united in 1990.

economy.industries: crude oil production and petroleum refining; small-scale production of cotton textiles, leather goods; food processing; handicrafts; aluminum products; cement; commercial ship repair; natural gas production
economy.exports: gold, fish, scrap iron, shellfish, industrial acids/oils/alcohols (2023)

partyFact.title: A waterfall you can see before you see it
partyFact.text: The spray from Victoria Falls can be visible more than 20 kilometres away. The Zambezi plunges through basalt gorges, producing the mist behind its name Mosi-oa-Tunya.

history.text: British South Africa Company control expanded in the 1890s. Northern Rhodesia came under direct British colonial administration in 1924 and became independent as Zambia in 1964.

economy.industries: copper mining and processing, emerald mining, construction, foodstuffs, beverages, chemicals, textiles, fertilizer, horticulture
economy.exports: raw copper, refined copper, gold, precious stones, electricity (2023)

partyFact.title: A medieval city in southern Africa
partyFact.text: Great Zimbabwe was a major Shona trading centre between the eleventh and fifteenth centuries. Its extensive stone ruins challenge the idea that medieval urban history belongs only to Europe and Asia.

history.text: British South Africa Company rule began in 1890. Southern Rhodesia became a self-governing British colony in 1923. A white-minority government unilaterally declared independence in 1965, without international recognition; recognised independence as Zimbabwe came in 1980.

economy.industries: mining (coal, gold, platinum, copper, nickel, tin, diamonds, clay, numerous metallic and nonmetallic ores), steel, wood products, cement, chemicals, fertilizer, clothing and footwear, foodstuffs, beverages
economy.exports: gold, tobacco, nickel, minerals, diamonds (2023)
